paper.title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
paper.abstract: Recent agent benchmarks increasingly ground evaluation in executable environments, from code repair to web navigation, app APIs, and function calling. Yet completing consequential work beyond code requires more than producing a plausible response or valid tool call: agents must gather missing information over multiple turns, follow domain policies, coordinate dependent tools, and realize the correct persistent state transition without collateral effects. In this paper, we introduce Thinkingbox,

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“agent 会不会调工具”，而是“agent 能不能在有持久后果的业务流程里稳定把事情办成”。现有很多 benchmark 主要检查答案表面是否合理、tool call 是否可执行，或者单步 API 选择是否正确，但对真实业务里更关键的部分覆盖不够：多轮澄清、策略约束、跨工具依赖、最终数据库状态是否正确、有没有多做或错做副作用。Thinkingbox 把这类任务形式化为一个可复现的 tool-agent-user 闭环环境，并把评测目标从‘轨迹像不像’转到‘终态和副作用对不对’。
summary.importance: 它对预训练本身不是直接方法贡献，更接近 agent reliability 评测基础设施。但对基座研究仍有两点启发。第一，它把“成功一次”和“稳定成功”明确拆开，用 pass@1、pass@k、pass^k 去量化发现能力与可靠性之间的差距，这对理解模型在长链交互中的策略稳定性、状态跟踪能力、以及训练信号是否足够约束很有帮助。第二，它把评测对象从代码和网页扩展到 stateful business workflow，这类环境更接近企业内真实工具链，也更容易暴露语言模型在长期状态维护、确认流程、策略遵循上的短板。贡献量级主要在 benchmark 和 sandbox 设计，不在新模型或新训练范式。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上分两层。第一层是 Thinkingbox sandbox。它把任务定义为一个有限时域的 POMDP：隐状态包含后端状态、模拟用户私有状态、评测相关事件日志和 episode 状态；agent 每一步只能看到对话历史和工具返回，动作是给用户发消息或调用某个工具及参数。工具调用在隔离的 backend session 中执行，系统记录 side effects，并在结束后运行隐藏的 executable checks。这个设计的关键不是把参考轨迹写死，而是允许多条有效路径，只要最终 backend state、必要副作用和对话约束满足即可。

第二层是 Thinkingbox-bench。基于这个 sandbox，作者构建了 507 个任务，覆盖零售/电商、旅行与酒店、车险、新银行内部 IT 支持、咨询公司的 IT/HR 支持五个域。任务强调几类常见企业流程模式：先查记录再更新、需要用户补充信息、需要确认后才能执行不可逆操作、受 domain policy 约束的变更、以及多工具串联。评测上，绝大多数任务用终态 backend checks 判定，另有 30 个任务额外加了二值 rubric，检查最终回复是否包含必要披露、是否泄露不该说的信息、以及文字说明是否与实际执行结果一致。

作者还专门强调 reliability 统计方式。pass@k 衡量多次尝试里是否至少成功一次，更像“发现能力”；pass^k 衡量 k 次是否次次成功，更接近“可依赖性”。这个区分很重要，因为很多 agent 在随机性、提示微扰或工具返回变化下会出现明显不稳定，单看 best-of-k 会高估真实可用性。
summary.experiments:
实验核心结论很清楚：当前模型在这类 stateful workflow 上还有明显可靠性缺口。基准共 507 个任务，作者评测了 12 个 proprietary 和 open-weight 模型，并对每个任务重复运行 20 次。最强模型的 pass@1 为 65.36%，说明单次运行离可用还有距离；pass@20 达到 91.12%，说明很多任务并不是完全不会，而是偶尔能做对；但 pass^20 只有 25.25%，说明若要求 20 次都稳定成功，可靠性会大幅下滑。这个 discovery–reliability gap 是全文最重要的实验发现。

从任务设计看，评测不是只看最终一句话，而是检查 terminal backend state，因此能区分几类常见失败：查对了对象但改错字段；回复里说会处理但后端没改；少做一步必要更新；多做了不该做的副作用；没拿到确认就执行高风险操作；以及最终话术与实际执行结果不一致。文中还做了 evaluator 相关分析和 failure mode 拆解，用来说明 fluent tool use 与 reliable work completion 不是一回事。

摘要里没有给出更细的分域数字和逐模型排名细节，但从引言和结果概述已经足够看出 benchmark 的区分度：既不是简单 function calling，也不是纯对话任务，而是把状态正确性放在首位，因此能把模型的“偶然成功”与“稳定完成”拉开。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，不需要逐式推导。建议先看 Introduction，抓住作者到底在批评现有 agent benchmark 的什么缺口。然后看 Thinkingbox sandbox 的定义和 Figure 2，理解 agent、simulated user、tool backend、side-effect extractor、judge 是怎么串起来的。接着重点看 benchmark 构成、任务检查方式，以及结果部分里 pass@1 / pass@20 / pass^20 的对比，这几处基本决定了这篇工作的价值。

如果时间有限，优先看三块：1）任务判定为何采用 terminal state 而不是参考轨迹；2）为什么要把 reliability 单独定义成 pass^k；3）failure analysis 里哪些错误是语言能力问题，哪些是状态管理和策略执行问题。预计 25–35 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读。若你做 agent training 或 tool-use post-training，可以再细看 rubric 设计和 evaluator ablation，因为这些会直接影响训练目标怎么定义。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a gap that many agent benchmarks leave open: not whether an agent can emit plausible tool calls, but whether it can reliably complete consequential, stateful business workflows. In these settings, success depends on multi-turn clarification, policy compliance, coordination across dependent tools, and ending in the correct persistent backend state without unintended side effects. Thinkingbox is built to evaluate that full loop rather than surface-level response quality or call validity.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-method paper. Its value is as evaluation infrastructure for agent reliability. For foundation-model research, two aspects matter. First, it cleanly separates one-off success from dependable repetition through pass@1, pass@k, and pass^k, which is useful for studying policy stability, state tracking, and the brittleness of long-horizon interaction. Second, it expands executable evaluation beyond code and web tasks into stateful enterprise workflows, where failures in confirmation, policy following, and backend consistency become visible. The contribution is meaningful on the benchmark/sandbox side, not on model architecture or training.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The work has two layers. The first is the Thinkingbox sandbox. A task is instantiated as a finite-horizon POMDP whose latent state includes backend state, simulated-user private state, evaluator-relevant event logs, and episode status. At each turn, the agent observes dialogue history and tool outputs, then either sends a user-facing message or issues a tool call with arguments. Tool calls execute inside isolated backend sessions. The system records side effects and runs hidden executable checks at the end. A key design choice is outcome-based evaluation: multiple trajectories may be valid as long as the final backend state, required side effects, and dialogue constraints are correct.

The second layer is Thinkingbox-bench, a 507-task benchmark spanning retail/e-commerce, travel/hospitality, auto insurance, neobank internal IT support, and consulting IT/HR support. Tasks are designed around recurring enterprise patterns: lookup-then-update flows, user clarification, confirmation before irreversible actions, policy-conditioned changes, and multi-tool coordination. Most tasks are graded through executable checks over terminal backend state. An additional subset of 30 tasks uses binary rubrics on the final response, covering required disclosures, confidentiality, and consistency between what the agent says and what it actually executed.

The reliability framing is central. pass@k measures whether at least one of k attempts succeeds, which captures discovery capability. pass^k measures whether all k attempts succeed, which captures repeatable reliability. That distinction is important because many agents can occasionally find a correct trajectory while remaining unstable under sampling noise or interaction variation.
summary_en.experiments:
The main empirical result is a large discovery–reliability gap. The benchmark contains 507 tasks, and the authors evaluate 12 proprietary and open-weight models with 20 repeated trials per task. The strongest model reaches 65.36% pass@1, which is still far from dependable single-run performance. Its pass@20 rises to 91.12%, showing that many tasks are solvable at least once. But its pass^20 is only 25.25%, meaning only a quarter of tasks succeed in all 20 attempts. That gap is the central takeaway of the paper.

Because evaluation is tied to terminal backend state rather than a single final answer, the benchmark can expose failure modes that simpler tool-use benchmarks miss: updating the wrong entity, producing a convincing response while leaving the backend unchanged, missing a required side effect, introducing an extra side effect, executing high-impact actions before collecting confirmation, or generating a final message inconsistent with the actual execution outcome. The paper also includes evaluator ablations and failure analyses to show that fluent tool use is not the same as reliable work completion.

The provided excerpt does not include the full per-domain or per-model breakdown, but the headline numbers already show strong benchmark discrimination: this is neither plain function-calling nor pure dialogue evaluation; it is outcome-centric stateful execution.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction to understand the exact limitation it identifies in current agent benchmarks. Then read the sandbox formulation and Figure 2 to see how the agent, simulated user, tool backend, side-effect extractor, and judges are composed. After that, focus on the benchmark construction and the result tables comparing pass@1, pass@20, and pass^20. Those sections carry most of the signal.

If time is limited, prioritize three questions: why terminal-state evaluation is preferred over reference trajectories, why reliability is defined separately from best-of-k success, and which failure modes come from language competence versus state management and policy execution. A useful first pass should take about 25–35 minutes. If you work on agent training or tool-use post-training, the rubric design and evaluator ablations are worth a closer read because they affect how one might define training targets.

recommendation.zh: 看任务设计和 executable checks；它比普通 tool-call benchmark 更能暴露长程状态错误。
recommendation.en: Read the task design and executable checks; this is more diagnostic for long-horizon state errors than ordinary tool-call benchmarks.

paper.title: StartupBench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Agents on Market-Validated End-to-End Workflows
paper.abstract: Recent advances in Large Language Models(LLMs) and agents have substantially improved the ability of AI systems to execute complex tasks. Yet existing benchmarks largely rely on researcher-selected tasks, leaving uncertain whether such progress extends to the work that real-world users actually demand from AI systems. We introduce \textbf{StartupBench}, an E2E agent benchmark grounded in market-validated AI startup products. Rather than defining tasks from pre-defined assumptions about useful ag

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解决的不是“模型会不会做某个子任务”，而是更难也更贴近真实使用的问题：通用 agent 能否在现实工作流里，按完整需求交付可用成品。作者认为现有 agent benchmark 的主要缺口有两个。第一，任务往往由研究者主观设计，未必对应真实用户已经愿意付费或持续使用的工作。第二，评测粒度过粗，常把复杂 deliverable 压成一个整体分数，难以判断模型到底是败在功能缺失、结构错误、格式不合规，还是领域知识不足。StartupBench 因而把任务来源改成“市场验证过的 AI-native startup 产品工作流”，并把评测单位改成“面向交付物的细粒度 rubric”。
summary.importance: 对基座模型研究的意义不在于提出新训练方法，而在于给 agent 能力提供了一个更接近真实需求分布的外部测量面。它的价值主要有三层。第一，它把 benchmark 的任务分布从研究者想象的 useful tasks，转成已经被市场筛过一轮的 delegated workflows，这对判断模型能力缺口更有约束力。第二，它强调 deliverable-level evaluation，而不是只看过程轨迹或单点答案，这对 post-train、tool use、长上下文规划都有直接影响。第三，它给出了一个很清楚的失败归因框架：当前系统的主要瓶颈不是“完全不会调用工具”，而是复杂指令遵循、跨约束一致性、领域专业性和成品质量控制。这些结论会反过来影响预训练和中后训练的数据构造：如果训练信号主要奖励局部正确，而不是完整交付，模型在真实工作流里就会系统性掉链子。
summary.technical_approach:
方法上，作者没有直接从公开 demo 抽任务，也没有纯手工编题，而是做了一个多阶段构建流程。第一步，筛选 AI-native startup，要求有一定融资和真实采用证据，用它们作为“用户确实愿意把这类工作交给 AI”的外部信号。第二步，访谈深度用户，恢复真实使用场景中的任务目标、输入条件、约束、期望交付物和验收标准。第三步，由领域专家把这些场景抽象成可复现、可回答、可评测的 benchmark 实例。第四步，做多轮质量控制，检查 realism、answerability、evaluability 和 discriminative difficulty。最终形成 97 个任务，覆盖 6 个主要领域。

评测设计上，核心不是单一总分，而是每个任务配多维 rubric，分别覆盖功能、结构、格式和领域特定质量。这样做的原因很直接：真实工作产品往往不是“答对就行”，而是要同时满足多个约束。若只做整体打分，模型可能在某一维严重失真，但被其他维度掩盖。作者还构建了统一的 agent harness 来跑代表性模型，尽量控制工具接口和执行环境，减少“某个系统工程实现更好”对结论的干扰。这个 benchmark 的方法创新不在算法，而在任务来源、任务抽象和评测协议三者绑在一起，形成了一个更像真实委托工作的评测闭环。
summary.experiments:
关键结果是：在统一 agentic harness 下，最强模型的成功率也只有约 30%。这说明当前通用 agent 距离“稳定交付专业可用成品”还有明显距离，而不是只差一点 prompt engineering。分领域看，Finance、STEM & Computer Science、Education & Humanities 更难，说明高约束、高专业性、强结构化输出的任务仍是明显短板。

从论文给出的分析框架看，失败主要集中在几类：一是复杂 instruction following，模型能理解大方向，但难以同时满足多条细约束；二是 domain-specific expertise，不是泛泛写作能力不足，而是在专业内容、术语、规范和推理链条上不稳；三是 deliverable completion，模型可能能产出“像样的草稿”，但离可直接使用的成品还有差距。虽然摘要里没有展开所有模型和每个 domain 的完整数字，但全文重点不是刷榜，而是证明：当任务来源更真实、评分更细时，现有系统的能力上限会显著低于常见 benchmark 给人的印象。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时建议先看 Introduction 和 StartupBench 构建流程，重点理解作者为什么不用传统 researcher-designed tasks，也为什么不用直接抓 startup demo。这里决定了 benchmark 的可信度。然后看任务构建与 rubric 设计部分，关注每个任务如何保证可回答、可评测、且仍保留真实工作流的复杂性。再看实验总表和按领域拆分结果，重点不是记住谁排第一，而是看不同领域失败模式是否一致。最后看 error analysis，尤其是作者如何把失败归因到 instruction following、领域知识和交付物质量，而不是笼统地说“agent 还不够强”。如果时间有限，30 到 40 分钟足够抓住主线；若要判断它是否适合作为内部评测基线，则需要细读 rubric 和质量控制流程。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a harder and more practical question than standard agent benchmarks: can a general-purpose agent produce professionally usable end-to-end deliverables under realistic constraints? The authors argue that many existing benchmarks are limited in two ways. First, tasks are often researcher-selected rather than grounded in workflows that users have already shown willingness to adopt or pay for. Second, evaluation is usually too coarse relative to the deliverable itself, making it hard to tell whether failure comes from missing functionality, poor structure, formatting violations, or lack of domain expertise. StartupBench addresses both by sourcing tasks from market-validated AI-native startup workflows and evaluating them with fine-grained rubrics tied to the final deliverable.
summary_en.importance: Its value for foundation-model research is not a new training recipe but a more realistic measurement surface for agent capability. There are three concrete contributions. First, it shifts the task distribution from researcher-imagined usefulness to workflows already filtered by market demand, which gives stronger external validity. Second, it evaluates complete deliverables rather than intermediate steps or loosely judged outputs, which matters for post-training, tool use, planning, and long-context systems. Third, it offers a sharper failure decomposition: current systems are not mainly blocked by the inability to call tools, but by complex instruction following, consistency across many constraints, domain expertise, and final-product quality control. That diagnosis is relevant upstream: if training signals reward local correctness more than complete deliverable quality, models will predictably underperform on real delegated work.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The benchmark construction pipeline is the main technical contribution. Instead of directly scraping product demos or manually inventing tasks, the authors use a multi-stage process. They first identify AI-native startups with evidence of funding and real adoption, using that as a proxy that users genuinely delegate these workflows to AI. They then interview deep users to recover actual usage contexts, task goals, inputs, constraints, expected deliverables, and acceptance criteria. Domain experts convert those validated scenarios into benchmark instances that are reproducible, answerable, and evaluable. A final quality-control stage checks realism, answerability, evaluability, and discriminative difficulty. The result is a 97-task benchmark spanning six major domains.

The evaluation protocol is equally important. Each task is scored with multiple independent rubrics covering functionality, structure, formatting, and domain-specific quality, rather than a single holistic score. The reason is straightforward: real work products must satisfy several coupled requirements at once, and a single score can hide severe failure on one dimension. The authors also evaluate representative models under a unified agentic harness to reduce confounding from system-specific tooling. The novelty here is not an algorithmic method but the coupling of task sourcing, task abstraction, and deliverable-level evaluation into one coherent benchmark design.
summary_en.experiments:
The headline result is that even the strongest model completes only about 30% of tasks under the unified harness. That is a strong signal that current general-purpose agents are still far from reliably producing professionally usable deliverables. Performance varies substantially by domain, with Finance, STEM & Computer Science, and Education & Humanities emerging as especially difficult. This suggests that high-constraint, expertise-heavy, and strongly structured tasks remain major weaknesses.

The paper’s analysis points to a few recurring failure modes. One is complex instruction following: models often capture the broad objective but fail to satisfy many detailed constraints simultaneously. Another is domain-specific expertise: the issue is not generic fluency, but instability in professional content, terminology, conventions, and reasoning. A third is deliverable completion: systems can often produce something plausible-looking, yet still fall short of a directly usable final product. The emphasis is less on leaderboard separation and more on showing that once task sourcing becomes more realistic and scoring becomes more faithful, the apparent capability ceiling of current agents drops materially.
summary_en.reading_guide: Start with the introduction and the benchmark construction section. The key question is why the authors reject both traditional researcher-designed tasks and direct extraction from startup demos. That design choice determines the benchmark’s credibility. Then read the task construction and rubric sections carefully, focusing on how they preserve real workflow complexity while keeping tasks answerable and evaluable. After that, look at the main results table and the domain breakdown. The useful signal is not who ranks first, but whether failure patterns are stable across domains. Finally, read the error analysis, especially the parts that separate instruction-following failures from domain-knowledge failures and final-deliverable quality issues. A quick pass takes around 30 to 40 minutes. A deeper read is needed if you want to judge whether this benchmark is suitable as an internal evaluation target.

recommendation.zh: 一个基于真实 AI 初创产品工作流的 Agent Benchmark，评估视角新颖，有助于了解当前模型在实际商业落地中的能力瓶颈。
recommendation.en: An agent benchmark based on real AI startup product workflows; offers a novel evaluation perspective and helps identify capability bottlenecks of current models in actual commercial deployments.

paper.title: Governance at the Boundary: How Agent Decomposition Degrades Policy Compliance
paper.abstract: Existing agent benchmarks ask whether the agent finished the task. We ask whether it finished it within policy. We introduce Fiducia-bench, a benchmark for the governability of financial agents---whether they escalate when obligated, abstain when required, and leave an auditable trail---and use it to study a question no prior benchmark addresses: does decomposing an agent into components degrade its governance? It does, and the mechanism is specific. Policy-relevant facts discovered by one compo

summary.core_problem: 这项工作研究 agent 从单循环结构拆成 orchestrator-subagent 结构后，政策合规能力是否下降，以及下降是否来自组件交接时的关键信息丢失。
summary.importance: 这不是预训练方法论文，但对通用 agent 评测和 post-train 信号设计有实际参考。它把“任务完成”与“按规则完成”分开，并指出多组件架构的风险不一定来自某个组件显式违规，而可能来自 policy-relevant facts 在 handoff summary 中被弱化或遗漏。这个问题会影响 agent SFT/RL 数据构造、轨迹级 verifier、工具调用审计和多代理系统训练。对基座研究员的启发是：如果训练信号只奖励最终任务成功，模型可能学不到跨边界传播约束的能力；需要把事实发现、事实传递、义务触发和工具调用后果拆开评估。
summary.technical_approach: 论文提出 Fiducia-bench，一个面向金融 KYC/AML 场景的 governability benchmark。环境是 seeded JSON store，工具确定性执行，所有 tool call 由环境记录 actor、参数和结果摘要，避免 agent 自报日志。政策以 YAML policy pack 表示，每条规则包含 rule_id、severity、自然语言文本和机器可检查 specification。当前规则有 10 条，覆盖 require_before、allow_list、state_assert、forbid_when 四类检查。验证器通过 replay trajectory 在 fresh environment 上复现每一步，在工具调用发生时检查触发条件，而不是只看最终状态。核心指标包括 governed success、constraint propagation loss、fact attenuation、violation locus 和 authority diffusion。fact attenuation 检查的是：某个触发事实已经被一个组件发现，但在跨组件 handoff 的 present_in token 中消失，导致后续组件没有执行应有动作或执行了禁止动作。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖 626 个 episode，主要网格是 {D0, D1, D2} × P0 × 100 task variants，使用两个模型，并额外测试 D0 下 P0/P1 policy access。D0 是单循环基线，没有组件边界；D1 和 D2 引入不同程度的分解。任务来自 5 个 seed scenarios，通过 persona、jurisdiction、amount、ownership percentage 等字段生成 100 个变体。结果很清楚：D0 在两个模型上 fact attenuation 为 0，因为没有边界。Qwen2.5-32B 在 D1 下丢失 56% 已发现事实，在 D2 下丢失 85%；gpt-4.1-mini 的对应比例为 3% 和 6%，绝对值低很多，但分解带来更高丢失的顺序仍然成立。一个有意思的现象是，Qwen2.5-32B 的 D2 结构发现 trigger facts 的次数高于 D0，27/100 对 16/100，但 D2 又把其中 22 个事实在交接中丢掉。也就是说，结构化委派提高了发现率，却降低了传播率。成对任务 kyc-0004 和 kyc-0005 显示，同一类事实丢失会造成相反合规错误：丢风险事实导致 under-escalation，丢免责事实导致 over-escalation。整体 governed success 只有 8/596，说明当前设置较难，也提示 benchmark 更适合分析失败机制，而不是只看通过率。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，预计 25–35 分钟。重点看 Benchmark Design 和 Metrics，这两部分比 KYC/AML 场景本身更有价值。需要关注三个设计细节：环境拥有 audit log，policy rule 可机器检查，trajectory replay 在每一步状态上验证。实验部分重点看 Table 4、Figure 1 和 Table 5：Table 4/Figure 1 给出不同架构下 fact attenuation 的主结果，Table 5 展示同一传播失败如何产生 under- 与 over-escalation。附录的 prompts 和 per-arm counts 可快速扫一眼，主要用于判断 prompt confound 和样本量是否影响结论。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies whether decomposing an enterprise agent into orchestrator-subagent components reduces policy compliance, and whether the failure mode is loss of policy-relevant facts at handoff boundaries.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent evaluation paper rather than a pretraining paper, but it is useful for post-training and agent-training signal design. It separates task completion from governed task completion, and shows that violations can arise even when no single component appears locally malicious or incompetent. The missing piece is often constraint propagation: a fact is discovered by one component, summarized away at a boundary, and never reaches the component that must act on it. This has implications for SFT/RL trajectory data, verifier design, audit logging, and multi-component agent training. Rewarding only final success will not teach models to preserve obligations across component boundaries.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors introduce Fiducia-bench, a governability benchmark for financial KYC/AML agents. The environment is a deterministic seeded JSON store with tool calls logged by the environment itself, including actor attribution, arguments, and result digests. Policies are encoded as YAML packs with rule IDs, severity, natural-language text, and machine-checkable specifications. The current pack contains 10 rules implemented through require_before, allow_list, state_assert, and forbid_when checks. Verification replays each trajectory against a fresh environment and evaluates trigger conditions at the state where each tool call occurred, rather than only inspecting the final state. The main metrics are governed success, constraint propagation loss, fact attenuation, violation locus, and authority diffusion. Fact attenuation is measured when a trigger fact is discovered but disappears from the handoff path before the component that must act on it.
summary_en.experiments: The study reports 626 episodes. The main grid is {D0, D1, D2} × P0 × 100 task variants across two models, with additional D0 P0/P1 policy-access tests. D0 is a single-loop baseline with no component boundary; D1 and D2 add decomposition. The benchmark contains 100 variants generated from 5 seed scenarios by varying personas, jurisdictions, amounts, and ownership percentages, including data-driven flips such as 26% versus 24% ownership. The main finding is boundary-sensitive attenuation. D0 has 0% fact attenuation for both models. On Qwen2.5-32B, D1 drops 56% of discovered facts and D2 drops 85%. On gpt-4.1-mini, the rates are much lower, 3% and 6%, but the ordering remains the same. Qwen2.5-32B under D2 discovers trigger facts more often than D0, 27/100 versus 16/100, yet drops 22 of the 27 discovered facts during handoff. Paired tasks kyc-0004 and kyc-0005 show that the same attenuation mechanism can produce under-escalation when a risk fact is dropped, or over-escalation when an exculpating fact is dropped. Overall governed success is 8/596, so the benchmark is more informative as a failure-mechanism probe than as a simple pass-rate leaderboard.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 25–35 minutes. The most useful parts are Benchmark Design and Metrics. Pay attention to three engineering choices: audit logs are owned by the environment, policy rules are machine-checkable, and verification is done by trajectory replay at the relevant historical state. In the results, read Table 4, Figure 1, and Table 5. Table 4 and Figure 1 contain the main attenuation comparison across architectures; Table 5 shows how the same handoff failure creates opposite compliance errors. The prompt appendix and per-arm counts are worth a quick check to assess prompt confounds and sample coverage.

recommendation.zh: 金融场景但结论通用：multi-agent 拆分在弱模型上造成严重的事实衰减，做 agent 架构的人应看 Table 的衰减率，别把 orchestrator 当免费午餐。
recommendation.en: Financial wrapping, general lesson: multi-agent decomposition causes severe fact attenuation on weaker models; check the attenuation table before treating orchestrators as a free lunch.

paper.title: WANDR: A Benchmark for Wide and Deep Research
paper.abstract: WANDR (Wide ANd Deep Research) is a benchmark of 500 realistic, challenging data-collection tasks for research agents. Each task requires a system to discover a large set of entities that satisfy specified criteria (breadth), investigate each entity through multiple coordinated web searches (depth), and return independently verifiable records with supporting sources and excerpts. Tasks are represented as qualification key hierarchies that specify the entities, relationships, evidence, and requir

summary.core_problem: 如何评测研究型 agent 在“宽且深”任务上的能力：既要大规模发现符合条件的实体集合（wide），又要对每个实体通过多轮检索建立可验证的事实（deep），并避免静态金标答案难以扩展、难以核验的问题。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接启发有限，但对 agent / 长程工具使用 / 检索推理的评测与 RL 训练信号设计有参考价值。其 reference-free、逐条证据核验、按层级聚合的 reward 设计，可作为 agentic post-training 与可验证奖励构造的样例；对基座能力评估也提供了一个比单问答更接近真实知识工作的任务形态。
summary.technical_approach: WANDR 把任务表示为 qualification key hierarchy（如 company(n) → employee(m) → url(k)），目标是产出 n×m×k 条可独立核验的记录。每条记录包含 URL 和原文摘录，评测时由 task-specific judge 重新抓取页面，判断页面与摘录是否满足任务约束，再聚合为 precision / recall / F1，并区分 soft（部分得分）和 hard（二值）两种口径。任务构造走半自动流水线：自动写作检查、可行性审计、judge 审计，可选人工复核，因此不需要预先标注完整金标集。论文还把失败模式定位到树的不同层级（实体发现、实体丰富、页面识别、证据抽取、实体消歧），并讨论了该任务作为 RL 环境的可扩展性：per-record verdict 提供密集奖励，层级计数提供课程难度梯度，流式 grader 可在训练 batch 间摊销重复抓取成本。
summary.experiments: Benchmark 含 500 个任务，规模从数十到数千条记录。对比了 Search as Code（agent 组合可编程检索原语）与传统的并行 subagent 固定端点 search-and-read 系统。最强的 SaC 系统仅达到 0.363 soft F1 和 0.133 hard F1，说明任务对前沿研究 agent 仍有明显区分度。论文还归纳了 volume collapse、snippet reliance、约束非系统性应用、cross-reference 跳过、过早停止、缺失丰富化、上下文溢出等典型失败模式。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，建议重点看 Section 3（qualification key hierarchy 与失败定位）、Section 5（reference-free grading 与 soft/hard 指标）以及 Appendix N（作为 RL substrate 的 reward 与课程设计）。评测协议和奖励构造部分对做 agent RL / verifier 的读者更有用，任务构造流水线可快速浏览。预计 20–30 分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: How to evaluate research agents on tasks that are both wide—discovering a large set of qualifying entities—and deep—establishing verifiable facts about each entity through orchestrated web searches—without relying on a static, exhaustively annotated gold answer set.
summary_en.importance: Limited direct relevance to pretraining, but useful for agent evaluation, long-horizon tool use, and RL reward design. Its reference-free, per-record evidence verification and hierarchical metric aggregation offer a concrete pattern for verifiable rewards in agentic post-training. The task shape also probes base-model capabilities closer to professional knowledge work than single-answer QA.
summary_en.technical_approach: WANDR represents each task as a qualification key hierarchy, e.g. company(n) → employee(m) → url(k), targeting n×m×k independently verifiable records. Each record cites a live page with verbatim excerpts. A task-specific judge re-fetches the page and checks whether the page and excerpts satisfy the substantive constraints, then aggregates verdicts into precision, recall, and F1 in both soft (partial credit) and hard (binary) forms. Task construction uses a semi-automated pipeline—authoring checks, feasibility audit, judge audit, and optional human review—so no complete gold set must be annotated. Failures are localized across the tree: entity discovery, entity enrichment, page identification, evidence extraction, and identity disambiguation. The benchmark is also designed as an RL substrate: per-record verdicts give dense partial-progress rewards, per-level counts provide a curriculum gradient, and a streaming cache-aware grader amortizes overlapping fetches across training batches.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark contains 500 tasks requiring dozens to thousands of records. It compares Search as Code, where agents compose programmable retrieval primitives, against conventional systems that run fixed-endpoint search-and-read loops across parallel subagents. The strongest SaC system reaches only 0.363 soft F1 and 0.133 hard F1, leaving substantial headroom even for frontier research agents. Recurring failure modes include volume collapse, snippet reliance, non-systematic constraint application, skipped cross-referencing, premature stopping, missing enrichment, and context overflow.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim. Focus on Section 3 for the qualification-key hierarchy and failure localization, Section 5 for reference-free grading and soft/hard metrics, and Appendix N for the RL-substrate design, especially dense rewards and curriculum structure. The task-construction pipeline can be read quickly. Estimated 20–30 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 比静态 QA benchmark 更贴近真实 research agent 的评测，judge 重抓页面验证是亮点；看任务结构和 judge 设计即可。
recommendation.en: Closer to real research-agent workloads than static QA, and the refetch-and-verify judge is the main novelty; read the task schema and judge design, skip the leaderboard.

paper.title: Act2Intention: A Benchmark For Developing Active Mobile Agents Through Inferring User Intention from GUI Actions
paper.abstract: Mobile GUI Agents powered by multimodal large language models (MLLMs) show promise in human-computer intelligence. However, current research primarily focuses on reactive task execution while lacking a comprehensive understanding-prediction-execution process for user intentions, which are the core requirements of active agents. In this paper, we propose the Act2Intention framework that builds an active mobile agent by integrating understanding, predicting user intentions, and executing decisions

summary.core_problem: 当前移动GUI Agent研究聚焦被动任务执行，缺乏面向主动Agent的用户意图理解-预测-执行全流程评估基准。
summary.importance: Benchmark贡献，构建了首个基于连续意图-动作轨迹的主动移动Agent评测基准，为主动Agent研究提供统一评测框架。
summary.technical_approach: 提出Act2Intention框架，包含三个模块：主动导向的意图理解、个性化主动意图预测、经验引导的意图执行；通过数据采集与验证式生成构建基准数据集，覆盖52个应用、7.2万+意图、70万+动作。
summary.experiments: 基于构建的基准数据集评测了多种多模态大模型和基线方法，所提Act2Intention Agent在主动服务任务上的表现优于现有基线。
summary.authors_note: 作者团队包括清华大学李永、西北工业大学于志文等，从事移动计算与人机交互研究。

summary_en.core_problem: Current mobile GUI Agent research focuses on reactive task execution, lacking a full-process evaluation benchmark for active agents covering user intention understanding, prediction, and execution.
summary_en.importance: Benchmark contribution; builds the first active mobile agent evaluation benchmark based on continuous intention-action trajectories, providing a unified evaluation framework for active agent research.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes the Act2Intention framework with three modules: proactive-oriented intention understanding, personalized proactive intention prediction, and experience-guided intention execution; constructs the benchmark dataset via data collection and validated generation, covering 52 apps, 72k+ intentions, and 700k+ actions.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluates multiple multimodal large models and baseline methods on the constructed benchmark; the proposed Act2Intention Agent outperforms existing baselines on proactive service tasks.
summary_en.authors_note: Author team includes Yong Li from Tsinghua University and Zhiwen Yu from Northwestern Polytechnical University, focusing on mobile computing and human-computer interaction.

recommendation.zh: 首个主动移动GUI Agent评测基准，做多模态Agent预训练可参考其评测设置，否则看摘要即可。
recommendation.en: First benchmark for active mobile GUI agents; useful for multimodal agent pretraining evaluation setup reference, otherwise read the abstract only.

paper.title: The Next Challenge for Agentic Cybersecurity: A Realistic, Contamination-Free Reverse Engineering Benchmark
paper.abstract: AI agents are rapidly improving in cybersecurity capabilities when the source code is available for analysis, yet much of the software most consequential to cybersecurity, including malware, firmware, and proprietary applications, is available only as binaries. Analyzing such software requires reverse engineering(RE): recovering program semantics before the analysis can be meaningfully performed. However, evaluating agentic RE poses a fundamental challenge: benchmark instances must be unseen as

summary.core_problem: 现有AI智能体的网络安全能力评测多基于源代码，但真实高价值目标（恶意软件、固件、专有软件）仅以二进制形式存在，需逆向工程（RE）能力支撑分析；现有RE基准无法同时满足两项核心要求：要么存在预训练数据污染（目标源码出现在训练语料中，模型靠识别而非真实分析得分，且RE场景下粗粒度污染的危害远高于其他安全任务的细粒度泄漏），要么采用CTF或玩具级程序，规模和反分析保护强度与真实软件不匹配，无法反映真实能力。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的具体启发包括两点：一是明确了预训练数据的粗粒度语义污染对专业能力评测的严重干扰，为预训练数据的去重、污染检测提出了更细分的专业场景要求；二是提供了一个无记忆捷径、难度匹配真实场景的专业能力基准，可用于验证LLM/Agent预训练后在低层级语义理解、抗混淆推理上的真实能力，而非依赖语料记忆的虚假性能。
summary.technical_approach: 投入5000+领域专家小时采用净室流程构建SRE-Bench：一是自研19个平均代码量16915.8行的私有程序，覆盖网络协议、固件、游戏、格式解析器、恶意软件5类真实RE高频场景；二是实现包含44种先进反分析原语的防护套件（总代码量27K+行，超半数原语无公开实现）。将私有程序与自研防护配置组合，生成262个无污染测试实例，每个实例配6项可确定性验证的任务，共1572个RE评测任务。
summary.experiments: 投入3.14万美元评测5个前沿模型，实验结果显示：性能最高的GPT-5.6-sol总体准确率仅61.4%，仅能完全恢复31.5%的实例；性能最低的模型无法完全恢复任何实例。自研反分析防护是核心瓶颈：使GPT-5.6-sol性能减半，其余模型性能降至接近0，原本的模型能力排名被拉平到近乎一致失效。模型失效模式与人类分析师存在显著差异：人类逆向的传统障碍（编译优化、链接处理）对模型影响极小，而符号剥离会带来显著性能损失，说明当前模型过度依赖词汇锚点而非深层语义理解。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议：先阅读第1章引言中关于RE场景污染特殊性的分析，再阅读第3章基准构建的净室流程与反分析套件设计，最后阅读第4章的模型评测结果与失效模式对比。预计阅读时间25-30分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Most existing cybersecurity agent evaluations rely on source code, but real high-stakes targets including malware, firmware and proprietary software are only available as binaries that require reverse engineering (RE) for analysis. Current RE benchmarks fail to meet two critical requirements simultaneously: they either suffer from pretraining data contamination (target source code appears in training corpora, letting models score via recognition instead of actual analysis, and coarse-grained contamination in RE is far more harmful than fine-grained leakage in other security tasks), or use CTF-style or toy programs that lack the scale and anti-analysis protection intensity of real-world software.
summary_en.importance: This work brings two concrete implications for pretraining research. First, it quantifies the severe distortion of coarse-grained semantic contamination in pretraining data on specialized capability evaluation, raising more granular scenario-specific requirements for pretraining data deduplication and contamination detection. Second, it provides a shortcut-free, realistically difficult benchmark that can measure true low-level semantic reasoning and anti-obfuscation capability of LLMs/agents, instead of spurious performance from corpus memorization.
summary_en.technical_approach: The team invested 5,000+ domain expert hours to build SRE-Bench via a clean-room pipeline. It includes 19 in-house private programs with an average of 16,915.8 lines of code, covering 5 high-frequency real RE domains: network protocols, firmware, games, format parsers, and malware. A comprehensive anti-analysis suite with 44 advanced protection primitives (27K+ LoC in total, over half of which have no public implementations) is also developed. Combining private programs and custom protection configurations yields 262 contamination-free instances, each attached with 6 deterministically verifiable tasks for a total of 1,572 RE evaluation tasks.
summary_en.experiments: Five frontier models were evaluated at a total cost of $31.4K. The highest-performing model GPT-5.6-sol reaches only 61.4% overall accuracy and fully recovers just 31.5% of instances, while the lowest-performing model cannot fully recover any instance. Custom anti-analysis protections are the core bottleneck: they halve GPT-5.6-sol's performance and drive all other models to near-zero, collapsing the original capability ranking into near-uniform failure. Model failure modes differ significantly from human analysts: classical obstacles for manual RE (compilation optimization, linking processing) have minimal impact on models, while symbol stripping incurs heavy performance losses, indicating current agents over-rely on lexical anchors instead of deep semantic understanding.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim recommendation: First read Section 1 for the analysis of contamination uniqueness in RE scenarios, then Section 3 for the clean-room benchmark construction pipeline and anti-analysis suite design, and finally Section 4 for model evaluation results and failure mode comparison. Estimated reading time: 25-30 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 无污染Agent基准的构建方法有参考价值，重点看§3数据构建与污染检测流程，可迁移到预训练数据去重验证。
recommendation.en: Contamination-free benchmark construction methodology is transferable; focus on §3 data building and contamination detection protocols, applicable to pretraining deduplication verification.

paper.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
paper.abstract: We introduce Video-DeepResearch (Video-DR), extending multimodal agents from static images to continuous video streams, a setting that demands dense spatiotemporal grounding coupled with open-web exploration. Preliminary evaluations reveal two critical bottlenecks in current models: (1) modality bias, where agents bypass visual tools in favor of textual search, and (2) parametric knowledge leakage, where models rely on internal memory rather than genuine tool-augmented execution. To address thes

summary.core_problem: 现有多模态深度研究Agent仅支持静态图像输入，无法适配连续视频流场景下的长时序多跳推理需求，且存在模态偏见（偏好文本搜索、回避视觉工具调用）和参数知识泄露（依赖内部记忆而非真实工具执行）两个核心瓶颈，同时缺乏适配该场景的训练数据构造管线和严格的评测基准。
summary.importance: 为视频类多模态基座的对齐训练提供了任务设计与数据构造的参考：感知-探索解耦的阶段式工具解锁机制可迁移至多模态Agent的后训练流程，用于缓解模态偏见；针对模态偏见、参数知识泄露的量化诊断方法，可用于通用多模态模型的对齐效果校验；强制双模态依赖的基准构造思路，也能避免评测被模型参数记忆污染。
summary.technical_approach: 将视频建模为关键实体轨迹的时序组合，设计Select_Keyframe（时序选帧）、Crop_Search（空间裁剪搜索）两类定制视觉工具，搭配标准网页搜索工具构成完整动作空间；采用解耦的感知-探索管线加阶段式工具解锁机制，强制Agent先完成跨帧视觉定位再执行网页检索，从训练流程上纠正模态偏见；训练采用两阶段管线：先监督微调，后接GRPO强化学习；同时搭建人机协同标注的VideoDR-Bench，共200个实例，每个问题都必须同时调用视觉搜索与外部知识推理才能解决，从根源上避免参数知识泄露；配套数据引擎产出30K视频定位QA对与7K人工校验的决策轨迹。
summary.experiments: 35B参数模型（Video-DeepResearch-35B-A3B）在VideoDR-Bench上准确率达64.0%，超过Claude-4.5-Sonnet的59.0%；30B参数变体准确率59.3%，与专有闭源基线持平；前置诊断实验显示，现有开源模型单任务平均仅调用0.10次视觉工具，同期文本搜索调用达1.27次，GPT-5在几乎零工具调用的情况下仍能达到57%准确率，直接验证了模态偏见与参数知识泄露问题的存在。
summary.reading_guide: 先浏览Introduction部分的两个瓶颈诊断实验（模态偏见、参数知识泄露的量化统计），再查看Method章节的阶段式工具解锁机制与数据引擎构造逻辑，最后扫读VideoDR-Bench的标注规则与准入标准，预计阅读时间20-25分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing multimodal deep research agents only accept static image inputs, failing to support long-horizon multi-hop reasoning in continuous video stream scenarios. They also face two critical bottlenecks: modality bias (preferring textual search over visual tool invocations) and parametric knowledge leakage (relying on internal memory instead of genuine tool execution), alongside a lack of suitable training data pipelines and rigorous evaluation benchmarks for this setting.
summary_en.importance: It provides practical references for alignment training of video-focused multimodal base models: the decoupled perception-exploration pipeline with stage-wise tool unlocking can be transferred to post-training workflows of multimodal agents to mitigate modality bias; the quantitative diagnostic methods for modality bias and knowledge leakage are applicable to alignment validation of general multimodal models; the benchmark construction logic that enforces cross-modal dependency also prevents evaluation contamination from model parametric memory.
summary_en.technical_approach: Video is modeled as a temporal composition of key entity trajectories. Two custom visual tools, Select_Keyframe for temporal frame selection and Crop_Search for spatial cropped visual search, are added to the action space alongside standard web search tools. A decoupled perception-exploration pipeline with stage-wise tool unlocking is implemented to force agents to complete cross-frame visual grounding before web retrieval, correcting modality bias through training workflow design. Training follows a two-stage recipe: supervised fine-tuning first, then Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) reinforcement learning. A human-AI collaborative benchmark VideoDR-Bench with 200 instances is built, where every question provably requires both visual search and external knowledge reasoning to eliminate parametric knowledge leakage. The supporting data engine produces 30K video-grounded QA pairs and 7K human-validated decision trajectories.
summary_en.experiments: The 35B parameter model (Video-DeepResearch-35B-A3B) reaches 64.0% accuracy on VideoDR-Bench, outperforming Claude-4.5-Sonnet which scores 59.0%; the 30B parameter variant achieves 59.3% accuracy, matching proprietary closed-source baselines. Pre-diagnostic experiments show existing open-source models invoke visual tools only 0.10 times per task on average, compared to 1.27 textual search calls, while GPT-5 attains 57% accuracy with nearly zero tool invocations, directly validating the existence of modality bias and parametric knowledge leakage.
summary_en.reading_guide: First review the quantitative diagnostic experiments for the two bottlenecks (modality bias, parametric knowledge leakage) in the Introduction, then check the stage-wise tool unlocking mechanism and data engine design logic in the Method section, and finally skim the annotation protocol and admission criteria of VideoDR-Bench. Estimated reading time: 20-25 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 多模态智能体从静态图扩展到视频流的代表性工作，GRPO训练策略和阶段工具解锁设计对多模态后训练有参考价值，重点看方法部分。
recommendation.en: Representative work extending multimodal agents from static images to video streams; the GRPO training strategy and stage-wise tool unlocking design offer reference for multimodal post-training, focus on the method section.

paper.title: AgentMemBench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Management Strategies in Conversational AI Agents
paper.abstract: Long-term memory remains a critical bottleneck for conversational AI agents, whose finite context windows cannot support coherent recall across thousands of turns. We present AgentMemBench, a unified, reproducible benchmark evaluating five memory management strategies under identical conditions: in-context windowing (ICW), external key-value store (EKV), graph-based episodic memory (GEM), compression-based summarisation (CBS), and web-augmented memory (WAM). All are assessed across three public

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是 conversational agent 的长期记忆评测问题：在有限上下文窗口下，不同记忆管理策略如何影响跨会话召回、回答质量、忠实性和部署开销。
summary.importance: 它不是预训练方法论文，更接近 agent memory 的评测资产。对基座研究员的启发在于，它把长上下文、检索记忆、摘要压缩、图结构记忆和外部 Web 记忆放在同一 harness 下比较，可以帮助判断哪些能力应该靠模型上下文长度扩展解决，哪些更适合交给外部 memory system。对 long-context pretrain 和 agent post-train 也有间接价值：如果训练或评测只看最终回答质量，而不看 memory footprint、token cost、latency 和检索 provenance，很容易高估某些记忆策略的实际可用性。
summary.technical_approach: AgentMemBench 统一实现并评测五类记忆策略：ICW，即 in-context windowing，只保留最近 k 个 token 或 turn；EKV，即 external key-value store，把历史片段编码成 embedding 后做近邻检索；GEM，即 graph-based episodic memory，从对话中抽取实体和关系，维护结构化记忆图；CBS，即 compression-based summarisation，用自然语言摘要压缩旧上下文；WAM，即 web-augmented memory，用 Web search 或 MCP 工具补充外部信息。评测覆盖三个公开数据集：LoCoMo 200 个问题 turn，MultiDoc2Dial 187 个问题 turn，MSC 104 个问题 turn，总计 491 个标注问题 turn，形成 5 种策略 × 3 类任务的 15 个配置。指标包括 Memory Recall@k、MRR、nDCG@k、Answer F1、LLM-judge Faithfulness，以及 token cost、latency、memory footprint 等部署效率指标。一个方法细节比较关键：每个检索结果都带有真实的 session/turn provenance，因此 Recall/MRR/nDCG 是按 gold-session 标注评分，而不是按检索索引做近似匹配。论文还把 MemGPT/Letta 和 HippoRAG 放进同一 harness，并提出 MADS，一个零样本 Memory-Adaptive Dynamic Selector，根据四个语料统计量选择记忆策略。
summary.experiments: 实验规模是 491 个标注问题 turn、3 个数据集、5 类主策略，并补充两个已有外部记忆系统。论文报告的总体趋势是：ICW 在需要召回很早会话时容易失败，因为相关信息已被截断；EKV 和 CBS 对长程事实召回更稳，前者依赖语义检索，后者依赖摘要是否保留关键信息；GEM 更偏 precision-over-recall，能提供结构化关联，但在信息抽取不完整或关系稀疏时会漏掉答案所需事实；WAM 更适合需要外部知识补充的场景，但它不等价于内部长期记忆，并引入额外延迟和工具调用成本。MADS 被定位为部署启发式，而不是保证最优的选择器；论文也分析了它与经验最优策略不一致的场景。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读 25–35 分钟。先看五类 memory strategy 的定义，确认各策略的输入、写入、检索和上下文拼接方式是否公平。然后看 provenance-aware retrieval evaluation 的指标设计，这是比普通 agent memory benchmark 更值得注意的部分。结果部分建议重点看不同数据集上的质量—成本权衡，而不是只看 Answer F1。MADS 部分适合快速浏览，主要价值在于把任务统计量和记忆策略选择联系起来；如果研究 long-context pretrain 或 agent memory training，可以重点关注哪些失败来自模型能力，哪些失败来自记忆写入和检索机制。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses long-term memory evaluation for conversational agents. The question is how different memory-management strategies behave when an agent must recall information across many sessions while operating under a finite context window.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent-memory benchmark rather than a pretraining contribution. Its relevance to foundation-model research is indirect but useful: it separates model context length from external memory design, and it evaluates not only answer quality but also retrieval quality, faithfulness, memory footprint, token cost, and latency. That matters for long-context training and agent post-training because a memory strategy that improves final-answer F1 may still be unattractive if it inflates context, retrieval latency, or tool-call cost.
summary_en.technical_approach: AgentMemBench implements five memory families under one harness. ICW keeps only a recent in-context window. EKV stores conversation snippets in an external key-value memory and retrieves them by dense similarity. GEM extracts entities and relations into an episodic knowledge graph, then retrieves structured neighborhoods. CBS compresses older context into natural-language summaries. WAM augments the agent with external web or MCP-style tool access. The benchmark uses three public datasets: 200 question turns from LoCoMo, 187 from MultiDoc2Dial, and 104 from MSC, for 491 annotated question turns in total. This yields 15 main configurations across five strategies and three task types. The metrics cover retrieval quality, including Memory Recall@k, MRR, and nDCG@k; answer quality, including Answer F1 and an LLM-judge faithfulness score; and deployment efficiency, including memory footprint, token cost, and latency. A notable design choice is provenance-aware retrieval evaluation: retrieved items carry true session/turn provenance, so retrieval metrics are computed against gold-session annotations rather than against ad-hoc retrieval indices. The paper also evaluates MemGPT/Letta and HippoRAG in the same harness and introduces MADS, a zero-shot dynamic selector that chooses a memory strategy from four corpus-level statistics.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark evaluates 491 annotated question turns across three datasets and five core memory strategies, with additional comparisons to published memory systems. The reported qualitative pattern is consistent with the expected failure modes of each design. ICW fails on questions whose evidence has fallen outside the recent window. EKV and CBS are stronger for long-range factual recall: EKV depends on semantic retrieval quality, while CBS depends on whether summaries preserve the needed details. GEM tends to be more selective, giving higher-precision structured recall but missing facts when extraction is incomplete or the graph neighborhood is sparse. WAM can help when external knowledge is needed, but it should not be treated as a replacement for internal conversational memory because it adds tool latency and cost. MADS is presented as a deployment heuristic rather than an optimal policy, and the paper explicitly examines cases where its selected strategy diverges from the empirically best one.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 25–35 minute skim is appropriate. Start with the definitions of the five memory strategies and check how memory is written, retrieved, and injected into the model context. Then read the provenance-aware metric design, since that is the cleanest methodological contribution. In the results, focus on quality-cost trade-offs across datasets rather than only final Answer F1. The MADS section is useful if the goal is to design adaptive memory policies. For long-context or agent-training work, the most useful lens is to separate model failures from memory-system failures: truncation, missing writes, weak retrieval, lossy summarization, and incomplete graph extraction have different implications for training data and architecture choices.

recommendation.zh: 读结果表就够；若 EKV 真压过 graph memory，很多复杂记忆系统要重新证明必要性。
recommendation.en: The result tables are enough; if EKV really beats graph memory, many complex memory systems need to re-justify their existence.

paper.title: MirrorCraft: Paired Evaluation under Hidden Rule Changes in Minecraft
paper.abstract: With the prosperity of the large language models (LLMs), it has become an interesting topic: how do LLM-based agents work in Minecraft? Unfortunately, most existing benchmarks evaluate them under fixed game mechanics. High performance in these settings does not show whether an agent can continue making progress when familiar recipes, drops, and other rules change. In this paper, we introduce MirrorCraft, a paired benchmark for evaluating agents under hidden rule changes in Minecraft. Each Mirror

summary.core_problem: 评估 Minecraft LLM agent 在游戏规则被隐藏修改后，是否还能持续推进任务，而不是只在固定规则下表现良好。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 agent benchmark。它把环境泛化从地形、资源和目标变化推进到 server-side rule changes，对检验 agent 是否真正能诊断规则变化有意义；对 LLM 基座预训练的直接启发较弱。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 MirrorCraft paired evaluation。每个 Mirror world 与 Vanilla world 配对，保持地形、出生点、资源位置、目标、接口和行动预算一致，只通过 datapack 修改合成配方、掉落等服务器规则，从而隔离隐藏规则变化带来的影响。
summary.experiments: 包含五个受控生物群系、六组规则套件、三类进度目标、两个模型家族和六种 agent 配置，统一使用 Mineflayer 接口。使用确定性的 advancement milestones 和 success 指标评估任务进展；摘要未给出具体分数和模型名称。

summary_en.core_problem: The benchmark tests whether Minecraft LLM agents can continue making progress when familiar game rules are secretly changed.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an agent evaluation benchmark. It shifts generalization testing from terrain or objective variation to server-side rule changes, which probes whether agents can diagnose altered dynamics rather than exploit memorized mechanics; the direct pretraining relevance is modest.
summary_en.technical_approach: MirrorCraft uses paired Vanilla and Mirror worlds. Each pair matches terrain, spawn, resource placement, objective, interface, and action budget, while datapacks modify recipes, drops, and other server-side rules to isolate hidden rule-change effects.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark covers five controlled biomes, six rule suites, three progression objectives, two model families, and six agent configurations under a shared Mineflayer interface. Progress is measured with deterministic advancement milestones and success metrics; the abstract does not report detailed scores or model identities.

recommendation.zh: 作为 agent 泛化评测备查即可；paired setup 干净，但 Minecraft 规则迁移离 pretrain 决策较远。
recommendation.en: Keep it as an agent-generalization benchmark reference; the paired setup is clean, but Minecraft rule transfer is far from pretraining decisions.

paper.title: RSIBench-Data: Benchmarking Data-Centric Research for Recursive Self-Improvement
paper.abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires turning evidence of model failures into better models. Data-centric post-training research entails diagnosing capability gaps, designing and validating training-data strategies, and learning from checkpoint feedback. Can LLM agents automate this loop? Existing benchmarks entangle research decisions with optimization, serving, evaluation, and systems implementation, obscuring agents' research capability. We introduce RSIBench-Data, a controlled benchmark of LLM

summary.core_problem: 现有递归自我改进相关基准混淆了Agent的数据研究能力与优化、服务、系统实现等变量，无法准确评测Agent自动迭代训练数据策略的能力
summary.importance: 提出首个控制变量的数据中心递归自我改进基准，将数据研究能力从其他系统变量中解耦，为自动改进模型训练数据的研究提供标准化评测环境
summary.technical_approach: 构建固定后训练栈，用Tinker提供训练服务、Harbor和E2B沙箱运行官方评测、固定各Agent的实验预算，让Agent仅能迭代修改目标模型的训练数据策略，不接触其他系统组件
summary.experiments: 在软件工程、终端使用、科学QA、数学共6个基准上评测4个前沿Agent，验证Agent具备基础的数据为中心研究能力，但迭代效率和效果仍有较大提升空间
summary.authors_note: 新加坡国立大学团队

summary_en.core_problem: Existing recursive self-improvement benchmarks entangle agents' data research capability with optimization, serving, and system implementation confounders, failing to accurately measure agents' ability to iteratively improve training data strategies.
summary_en.importance: Introduces the first controlled data-centric RSI benchmark that isolates data research capability from other system variables, providing a standardized evaluation environment for automated training data improvement research.
summary_en.technical_approach: Builds a fixed post-training stack with Tinker for training services, Harbor and E2B sandboxes for official evaluation, and fixed compute budgets across agents; agents can only revise training data strategies for the fixed target model without accessing other system components.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluates 4 frontier agents on 6 benchmarks spanning software engineering, terminal use, scientific QA and mathematics; agents demonstrate basic data-centric research capabilities but show large room for improvement in iteration efficiency and performance.
summary_en.authors_note: Team from National University of Singapore

recommendation.zh: 控制变量设计思路有参考价值，作为自动数据迭代方向文献备查，无需读全文
recommendation.en: The controlled variable design is worth noting, archive as literature for automated data iteration research, no need to read the full text.

paper.title: OmniaBench: Benchmarking General AI Agents Across Diverse Scenarios
paper.abstract: Large language models are increasingly evolving from text generators into general agents capable of understanding user requests, invoking external tools, and completing complex tasks through interaction. However, existing agent benchmarks often focus on limited scenarios, tool ecosystems, or interaction formats, making it difficult to systematically characterize model capabilities across heterogeneous application settings. We introduce OmniaBench, a benchmark for evaluating general agents across

summary.core_problem: OmniaBench 解决的是通用 Agent 评测覆盖不足的问题。现有工具调用、Web 环境、长程规划或专业工作流 benchmark 往往绑定少数场景、少数工具生态或固定交互格式，难以判断一个模型在真实应用分布中的泛化能力。论文试图把评测对象从单点任务扩展到带状态、带工具、可交互的多场景任务空间。
summary.importance: 这篇论文对基座预训练本身不是直接贡献，更接近 Agent 能力评测资产。它的启发在于：后训练阶段越来越依赖可诊断的交互式评测，而这类评测需要显式状态、工具执行和分维度能力拆解。对预训练研究员有用的部分，是它提供了一种观察模型“从语言能力到任务执行能力”缺口的框架，尤其适合分析模型在规划、状态跟踪、工具调用和可靠性上的瓶颈。但它不是训练方法论文，也不直接回答数据配比、优化或建模目标问题。
summary.technical_approach: OmniaBench 从真实应用生态构造场景 taxonomy。数据来源包括应用商店、产品需求文档、行业资料、Web 检索和人工修订，覆盖 ToC、ToB、ToE 三类使用环境，共 90 个一级领域和 354 个二级领域。每个领域进一步实例化为可交互环境，包含 tools、entities、states 和初始化配置。任务要求模型理解用户请求，在多轮交互中调用工具、维护环境状态，并完成目标。评测设计包含十个能力维度：任务理解、信息获取、规划与决策、状态管理、工具使用、代码与程序化操作、数据分析、办公与文档处理、交互协作、可靠性与安全。难度设计采用 compositional atomic difficulty，把用户意图、persona 约束、环境状态、工具执行、多轮交互和结果验证拆成可组合因素。评分侧结合 rubric checklist 和 VerifyCode，用于减少只看最终成功率带来的诊断盲区。
summary.experiments: 论文报告在该 benchmark 下，即使较强模型也远未接近满分。给出的整体分数中，Claude-Sonnet-5 为 58.54，GPT-5.6-Sol 为 57.14。这个结果主要说明任务集难度较高，且单一总分不足以解释失败来源，因此论文强调按领域、能力维度、任务复杂度、交互轮数和错误类型分解分析。由于提供内容中没有完整表格，无法确认各模型完整排名、样本规模、人工一致性指标和 VerifyCode 的通过率细节。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，预计 20–30 分钟。优先看 benchmark 构造流程、Figure 2、十维能力 taxonomy、atomic difficulty 设计和评测协议。结果部分重点看错误分析，而不是只看 overall score。对预训练研究更有信息量的问题是：哪些失败来自语言理解不足，哪些来自状态管理和工具执行；这些信号能否反向指导中训练或后训练数据构造。

summary_en.core_problem: OmniaBench targets the coverage gap in general-agent evaluation. Existing agent benchmarks often focus on a narrow set of scenarios, tool ecosystems, or interaction formats. This makes it hard to characterize whether a model can generalize across realistic applications that require state tracking, tool execution, and multi-turn interaction.
summary_en.importance: The paper is mainly an evaluation contribution rather than a pretraining-method contribution. Its value for foundation-model researchers is diagnostic: it offers a structured way to measure the gap between language competence and executable task completion. The most relevant signals are failures in planning, state management, tool use, and reliability, which can inform post-training data design and agent-oriented evaluation suites.
summary_en.technical_approach: OmniaBench builds a broad scenario taxonomy from app stores, product requirement documents, industry resources, web retrieval, and human refinement. The taxonomy spans ToC, ToB, and ToE settings, with 90 level-1 domains and 354 level-2 domains. These domains are instantiated into interactive environments with tools, entities, states, and initialization configurations. The benchmark decomposes agent ability into ten dimensions: task understanding, information gathering, planning and decision making, state management, tool use, code and programmatic operations, data analysis, office and document handling, interactive collaboration, and reliability/safety. It also defines compositional atomic difficulty factors, including user intent, persona constraints, environment states, tool execution, multi-turn interaction, and result verification. Evaluation combines rubric checklists with VerifyCode-style checks to support more fine-grained diagnosis than a single success rate.
summary_en.experiments: The reported overall scores suggest that current strong models still struggle on the benchmark: Claude-Sonnet-5 scores 58.54 and GPT-5.6-Sol scores 57.14 under the proposed protocol. The main experimental message is not the absolute ranking but the decomposition of failures by domain, capability dimension, complexity, interaction length, and error type. The provided content does not include the full result tables, sample counts, inter-annotator agreement, or detailed VerifyCode statistics.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. Focus on the benchmark construction pipeline, Figure 2, the ten-dimensional capability taxonomy, the atomic difficulty design, and the evaluation protocol. In the results, read the error analysis before the leaderboard. For pretraining and post-training researchers, the useful question is which failures are caused by missing knowledge or language understanding, and which are caused by state tracking, planning, or tool execution.

recommendation.zh: 只看 taxonomy、环境状态定义和任务合成流程；分数榜先别信，Agent benchmark 的可复现性通常是硬伤。
recommendation.en: Read the taxonomy, state specification, and task-generation pipeline; treat the leaderboard cautiously because agent benchmarks often fail on reproducibility.

paper.title: DevicesWorld: Benchmarking Cross-Device Agents in Heterogeneous Environments
paper.abstract: LLM-based agents have rapidly improved at operating individual digital environments such as mobile applications, desktop systems, and smart homes. However, real-world user goals often span multiple devices: information may come from a phone, be processed on a desktop, and the result may need to appear on another device. Most existing benchmarks center on a single dominant execution environment, making it difficult to evaluate whether agents can acquire and integrate information across heterogene

summary.core_problem: 现有agent评测多是单一环境，缺少对“跨设备协作/信息跨端流动”的可执行评测。
summary.importance: 核心贡献是可执行benchmark与统一评测框架（rule-based verifiers），对通用agent能力与工具使用评估有用；对预训练本身是间接价值（提供更贴近真实分布的交互式评测信号）。
summary.technical_approach: 构建DevicesWorld：把mobile/desktop/IoT三类环境整合到统一交互与评测框架；每个任务包含自然语言目标、参与设备与初始状态、可执行动作空间、以及基于规则的自动验证器。
summary.experiments: 数据规模为6,140个可执行任务。摘要未给出具体参评模型、对比基线与分数差距等结果细节。
summary.authors_note: Shanghai Jiao Tong University

summary_en.core_problem: Most agent benchmarks are single-environment; we lack executable evaluation for cross-device, dependency-heavy tasks.
summary_en.importance: Main contribution is an executable benchmark + unified evaluation framework with rule-based verifiers; indirectly useful for pretraining via more realistic interactive evaluation signals.
summary_en.technical_approach: DevicesWorld integrates mobile/desktop/IoT into one interaction and evaluation framework; each task specifies NL goal, devices and initial states, executable actions, and rule-based verifiers.
summary_en.experiments: 6,140 executable tasks. The abstract does not report model baselines or quantitative results.
summary_en.authors_note: Shanghai Jiao Tong University

recommendation.zh: 作为“跨设备agent”评测资产可备查；预训练研究员只需看任务定义与verifier设计，别指望从结果里得到干净的训练结论。
recommendation.en: Useful as a cross-device agent eval asset; skim task specs and verifier design—don’t expect clean training takeaways from the reported results.

paper.title: How Many Tasks Are Enough for Agent Benchmark Decisions? A Replay Analysis of Public LLM Agent Benchmarks
paper.abstract: Agent benchmarks often compare two agents after all tasks have run, but costly evaluations make partial runs tempting. A task fraction alone does not show whether a partial run supports the same pairwise conclusion as the completed benchmark. We study this question by replaying completed public task-level records from SWE-bench, AppWorld, and tau-bench. A partial budget counts as enough only when it supports the completed benchmark's decision, covers required task groups, and leaves no more than

summary.core_problem: 解决高成本 agent benchmark 中，跑多少任务子集才足以支持与完整 benchmark 一致的模型比较结论。
summary.importance: 这是评测统计与预算分配问题。对做大规模 agent eval、AI delegation eval 或内部 benchmark 设计的人有实际价值，但对基座预训练本身的直接启发有限。
summary.technical_approach: 作者对已完成的公开任务级记录做 replay analysis，在不同任务预算下重放部分任务结果，并要求同时满足三类条件：与完整 benchmark 的 pairwise decision 一致、覆盖必要任务组、未决比较比例低于阈值。核心是把“任务占比”转成“决策可靠性”问题。
summary.experiments: 在 SWE-bench、AppWorld、tau-bench 上做回放分析。摘要给出关键数字：在严格阈值下，AppWorld 约 15% 任务即可满足目标，tau-bench 约 25%，SWE-bench Verified 需要约 90%，SWE-bench Lite 在 95% 内仍无法满足主要覆盖规则。说明不同 benchmark 的任务冗余度和方差差异很大。

summary_en.core_problem: It studies how many tasks are needed in expensive agent benchmarks before a partial evaluation supports the same pairwise conclusion as the full benchmark.
summary_en.importance: This is an evaluation-statistics and budget-allocation paper. It is practically useful for people building internal agent evals, but only indirectly relevant to foundation-model pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper performs replay analysis on completed public task-level benchmark records. A partial run is considered sufficient only if it matches the full benchmark's pairwise decision, covers required task groups, and leaves no more than a target fraction of comparisons unresolved. The key shift is from task fraction to decision reliability.
summary_en.experiments: The analysis covers SWE-bench, AppWorld, and tau-bench. The abstract reports that under a strict threshold, AppWorld first satisfies all targets at 15% of tasks, tau-bench at 25%, and SWE-bench Verified at 90%, while SWE-bench Lite does not satisfy all targets by 95% under the primary coverage rule. This shows large variance in redundancy and stability across benchmarks.

recommendation.zh: 做内部 agent eval 可以记住这些数字，但它更像统计备忘录；知道 SWE-bench 不能随便抽样就够了，不必细读正文。
recommendation.en: Useful as an evaluation memo, not a deep methods paper; the main takeaway is that SWE-bench-style partial runs are far less reliable than people assume.

paper.title: PM-Bench: Evaluating Prospective Memory in LLM Agents
paper.abstract: A significant challenge in agentic AI is prospective memory: the ability to execute an intention at a specific future cue or state while other activities are ongoing. We introduce PM-Bench, a text-based benchmark for measuring prospective memory capabilities in modern LLM agents. Inspired by the Virtual Week paradigm from cognitive science, PM-Bench evaluates how well LLM agents maintain user intentions, execute delayed intentions, and monitor latent environment changes. Over the course of a sim

summary.core_problem: 评测 LLM agent 在长期交互中维持未来意图、在正确时机触发延迟任务的 prospective memory 能力。
summary.importance: 贡献是一个认知科学启发的 agent benchmark。它补了现有 agent eval 对长期意图保持、潜在环境监控和延迟执行能力覆盖不足的空白，但对预训练方法的直接推动有限。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 PM-Bench，一个文本环境中的七天模拟任务框架，借鉴 Virtual Week 范式。agent 需要在持续进行当前活动的同时，维护用户意图、监控环境状态变化，并在未来 cue 或状态满足时执行 deferred tasks。作者还比较了多种 agent 配置，分析不同 memory/strategy 设计的效果差异。
summary.experiments: 评测 8 个前沿模型和 8 种 agent 配置。摘要给出的关键结果是：最佳方法 GPT-5.4 agent 也只有 65.1% F1，且没有一种统一策略在所有模型上都占优。这说明 prospective memory 是当前 agent 的真实短板，而不是某个 prompt 小技巧能解决的问题。

summary_en.core_problem: It evaluates prospective memory in LLM agents: the ability to maintain future intentions and execute them at the right cue while other activities continue.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a cognitively motivated benchmark for agents. It fills a gap in current evaluations around delayed intentions, latent state monitoring, and long-horizon intention maintenance, but it is only indirectly relevant to pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces PM-Bench, a text-based seven-day simulation inspired by the Virtual Week paradigm from cognitive science. Agents must continue ongoing activities while remembering user intentions, monitoring latent environmental changes, and triggering deferred tasks when the right future cue or state appears. Multiple agent configurations are compared to probe strategy effects.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark evaluates eight state-of-the-art models under eight agent configurations. The headline result in the abstract is that the best setup, a GPT-5.4 agent, reaches only 65.1% F1, and no single improvement strategy dominates across models. This suggests prospective memory is a genuine weakness rather than something fixed by a simple prompting trick.

recommendation.zh: 如果你关心 agent 长程失败模式，这个 benchmark 值得记名；但它离 pretrain 很远，看 abstract 和主结果表就够。
recommendation.en: Worth knowing if you care about long-horizon agent failure modes, but it is far from pretraining; the abstract and main results table are enough.

paper.title: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench: Testing the Limits of Agents on Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks with Dense Reward-Based Grading
paper.abstract: AI agents have become capable of autonomously completing short, well-specified tasks. However, existing terminal benchmarks largely focus on simple problems that finish within minutes and are evaluated only by their final outcome. This setup overlooks intermediate progress and partial solutions, yielding sparse reward signals and an incomplete picture of agent capability. We introduce Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench, a terminal benchmark of 46 long-horizon tasks spanning nine categories, including e

summary.core_problem: 现有 terminal agent 评测多是短任务、终局打分，难以衡量 agent 在几十分钟到数小时工作流中的持续执行、错误恢复和自我验证能力。Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 试图把评测对象从“能否完成一个局部补丁”推进到“能否在长轨迹中稳定推进多个子目标”。
summary.importance: 这篇论文的主要价值在 eval，而不是直接的预训练方法。它对基座研究的启发在于：长程 agent 能力不能只靠最终 pass/fail 衡量，dense reward 能暴露中间进展、超时、过早停止、弱验证等不同失败模式。对于做 post-train、RL、test-time scaling 或 agent 数据合成的人，这类细粒度轨迹信号比终局标签更接近可训练反馈，也更容易定位模型缺陷。
summary.technical_approach: Benchmark 沿用 Terminal-Bench 的容器化 terminal 环境：每个任务包含自然语言指令、相关文件和工具、可从命令行执行的参考解法。主要改动是把任务拆成语义明确的子任务，并为每个子任务配置检查器，最终按子任务完成率给分，而不是只看最终状态是否通过。任务覆盖 46 个长程任务、9 个类别，包括实验复现、交互式游戏、软件工程、多模态分析、科学计算等。这个设计保留了真实 terminal 工作流中的读写文件、运行脚本、查看中间输出、迭代调试等过程，同时提供比二值测试更密的评测信号。
summary.experiments: 论文评测了 15 个前沿 agent 配置。Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 上的 rollout 平均达到 231 个 episodes、9.9M tokens、85.3 分钟墙钟时间，并在 90 分钟上限附近退出，明显长于 Terminal-Bench 和 SWE-Bench 这类更短的 terminal/code-editing 评测。即便采用子任务部分给分，当前系统表现仍然偏弱：最强配置 GPT-5.5 在 0.95 reward threshold 下成功率为 15.2%，所有模型平均 pass rate 为 4.3%。失败分析显示，很多失败不是局部步骤完全错误，而是无法持续推进、无法确认完成状态，或在预算内收尾失败。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，预计 25 到 35 分钟。优先看 benchmark 构造和 grading scheme，重点确认子任务如何拆分、检查器是否稳健、partial credit 是否会引入可投机路径。实验部分重点看各模型在 reward threshold 下的表现，以及 failure analysis 中对 timeout、premature stopping、self-verification failure 的区分。若关心 RL 或 agent 训练数据，可以进一步看 dense reward 是否适合转成过程监督信号。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a gap in terminal-agent evaluation: existing benchmarks are short and mostly final-outcome graded, so they do not measure whether agents can sustain progress, recover from errors, and verify completion over long terminal workflows.
summary_en.importance: Its contribution is primarily an evaluation asset. The useful signal for LLM training research is the dense grading setup: it separates partial progress from true completion and makes failure modes such as timeouts, premature stopping, and weak self-verification observable. This matters for post-training, RL, test-time search, and agent trajectory data construction, where binary final labels are often too sparse to guide improvement.
summary_en.technical_approach: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench follows the Terminal-Bench-style containerized task format: a natural-language instruction, files and tools inside a terminal environment, and a reference solution executable from the command line. The key change is subtask-based grading. Each task is decomposed into meaningful intermediate checks, and the agent receives credit according to the fraction of completed subtasks. The benchmark contains 46 tasks across nine categories, including experiment reproduction, interactive games, software engineering, multimodal analysis, and scientific computing.
summary_en.experiments: The paper evaluates 15 frontier agent configurations. Rollouts average 231 episodes, 9.9M tokens, and 85.3 minutes of wall-clock time before termination under a 90-minute timeout, making the benchmark substantially longer than common terminal and code-editing benchmarks. Current agents remain weak even with partial credit: the strongest reported setup, GPT-5.5, reaches 15.2% success at a 0.95 reward threshold, while the average pass rate across models is 4.3%. The analysis suggests that agents often fail by losing sustained progress or failing to verify completion, rather than by making every local step wrong.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 25–35 minutes. Focus on the task construction, subtask decomposition, and grading protocol. The most important experimental sections are the thresholded success rates and the failure analysis that separates timeout-driven incompletion from early stopping and self-verification failures. For RL or agent-data work, check whether the dense reward design could be reused as process supervision.

recommendation.zh: 长程Agent评测的重要资产，任务分解与密集奖励设计可直接用于预训练长程能力的对齐目标，重点看§3任务设计与评分协议
recommendation.en: Key benchmark for long-horizon agent evaluation; focus on §3 task design and grading protocol for pretraining long-horizon alignment targets

paper.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
paper.abstract: The rapid development of large language models and multimodal large language models has accelerated the emergence of proactive agents capable of operating everyday tools and assisting users in real-world environments. However, existing benchmarks struggle to evaluate such agents effectively, as they often rely on sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluation paradigms. Moreover, their scenario-based task taxonomies mix multiple model capabilities within the same task category, making it diff

summary.core_problem: 解决现有 proactive agent benchmark 过度依赖沙盒环境、单轮评测和混杂任务分类，导致难以定位 agent 失败根因的问题。
summary.importance: 这是 agent 评测资产。对预训练研究员的直接价值有限，但如果你关心真实环境中的 agent 能力分解、长上下文和跨平台协作评测，这类 capability-driven benchmark 有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 UniClawBench，一个面向真实世界 proactive agents 的能力驱动 benchmark。它围绕五类基础能力组织任务：Skill Usage、Exploration、Long-Context Reasoning、Multimodal Understanding、Cross-Platform Coordination，并设计 400 个双语真实任务，强调动态环境和更细粒度的能力归因。
summary.experiments: 摘要显示 benchmark 包含 400 个 bilingual real-world tasks，区别于以往 scenario-based taxonomies。论文的主要实验应是用若干 LLM/MLLM agents 在五类能力上做分项评测，分析不同模型在真实环境中的瓶颈。由于它是 benchmark 论文，关键不在模型规模，而在任务设计是否 clean、可复现、能否稳定区分能力短板。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自香港大学 MMLab。该团队在多模态与 agent 评测上有一定持续产出，但这篇更偏 benchmark 构建。

summary_en.core_problem: It addresses the limitations of existing proactive-agent benchmarks that rely on sandboxed environments, single-turn evaluation, and mixed task taxonomies, making failure attribution difficult.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent evaluation asset. Its direct value to pretraining researchers is limited, but it is useful if you care about capability decomposition for real-world agents, especially long-context reasoning and cross-platform coordination.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces UniClawBench, a capability-driven benchmark for proactive agents in real-world settings. It organizes tasks around five foundational capabilities: Skill Usage, Exploration, Long-Context Reasoning, Multimodal Understanding, and Cross-Platform Coordination, with 400 bilingual real-world tasks designed for dynamic environments and finer-grained diagnosis.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark contains 400 bilingual real-world tasks and explicitly departs from prior scenario-based taxonomies. The main experiments likely evaluate multiple LLM/MLLM agents across the five capability axes to identify bottlenecks in realistic environments. As a benchmark paper, the key question is not model scale but whether the task design is clean, reproducible, and diagnostically useful.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from HKU MMLab, a group with ongoing work in multimodal systems and agent evaluation, though this paper is primarily a benchmark contribution.

recommendation.zh: 如果你做 agent eval，可以扫一眼任务分解法；否则知道有这么个真实环境 benchmark 就够了，正文不必细读。
recommendation.en: If you work on agent eval, skim the capability decomposition; otherwise it is enough to know this benchmark exists without reading the full paper.

paper.title: AgentLens: Production-Assessed Trajectory Reviews for Coding Agent Evaluation
paper.abstract: We present AgentLens, a production-assessed benchmark for interactive code agents. Most code-agent benchmarks reduce a run to a single bit -- did the task pass? -- but the people who actually use these agents experience the entire trajectory: how the agent follows instructions, uses its tools, verifies its own work, recovers from mistakes, and talks to them along the way. AgentLens evaluates that whole trajectory. It pairs formal verification, where an objective check exists, with LLM-written tr

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是编码 Agent 评测对象定义不对的问题。现有 benchmark 往往只看任务最终是否通过测试，但真实产品使用中，用户感受到的是完整轨迹：是否理解需求、是否安全使用工具、是否会验证自己的修改、出错后能否恢复、最终沟通是否诚实清楚。AgentLens 把“完整交互轨迹”而不是“最终 pass/fail”作为主要评测对象，并试图把这种评测做成可复用、可解释、可用于生产回归检测的流程。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是直接贡献，但对 post-train、agent training 和模型行为诊断有现实价值。尤其是当基座模型越来越多地通过工具调用和多步交互暴露能力时，只看最终成败会掩盖很多训练信号质量问题。AgentLens 的启发在于：评测资产不只用于排榜，也可以反过来定义更细粒度的偏好数据、过程监督和回归监控指标。对于做 coding agent、tool-use SFT、trajectory preference modeling 的团队，这类 benchmark 比单一通过率更接近真实优化目标。
summary.technical_approach:
核心方法是 trajectory-level evaluation protocol。每次运行记录完整会话轨迹，包括用户消息、agent 回复、工具调用、文件编辑、命令执行、验证尝试、最终答复和仓库最终状态。评测时不只做 formal verification；在有客观检查的任务上保留自动验证，同时引入 LLM judge 对整条轨迹写文字 review，并按多个维度打分，例如 instruction following、tool discipline、validation behavior、error recovery、user-facing communication 等。这样做的关键不是简单加一个 judge 分数，而是把“可读解释”作为一等产物，让评测结果能用于诊断。

另一个重要设计是 side-by-side reviews。作者不仅单独评一条轨迹，还让 judge 比较两个 agent 或两个版本在同一任务上的完整表现，用于模型比较、feature evaluation 和 regression analysis。这比只看 aggregate score 更适合产品迭代，因为很多退化是局部行为变化，不一定立刻反映在最终通过率上。

任务构造上，AgentLens 使用 production-like interactive coding workflows，并引入 simulated user。这个 simulated user 由另一个 LLM 按 persona 和 task objective 驱动，借鉴了 τ-bench 一类“带隐藏目标的用户交互”设定。这样可以覆盖那些没有天然二值结果的任务，例如写文档、解释代码、整理项目结构等。论文还强调 reliability 和 bias checks，说明作者意识到 LLM-as-judge 的稳定性和偏差问题，至少在协议层面做了校验。
summary.experiments: 从给出的全文片段可以确认，实验包括四类内容：一是 leaderboard，比较当前模型在 AgentLens 上的表现；二是 qualitative analysis，分析不同 agent 在轨迹层面的行为差异，以及 review 能捕捉到哪些 pass/fail 指标看不到的问题；三是与公开 benchmark 的相关性研究，检验 AgentLens 分数与现有代码 agent 基准之间的关系；四是 nightly evaluation pipeline，用于持续监控一个活跃开发中的生产 coding agent 的回归。片段里没有给出具体模型名单、样本规模、评分维度权重、judge 一致性系数或相关系数数值，因此不能编造具体数字。真正值得看的是：LLM judge 的复现性如何，side-by-side 比较是否比绝对打分更稳定，formal verification 与 trajectory review 的相关和互补关系如何，以及 benchmark 是否能提前发现产品退化。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读到中度精读，重点不在模型方法，而在评测协议设计。先看 Introduction，明确它为什么反对把 code agent 压缩成单一 success bit。然后直接读 Section 3：任务集与 simulated user、trajectory review protocol、quality index、side-by-side reviews、reliability/bias checks、nightly pipeline，这些是核心。Section 4 主要看 qualitative examples 和 correlation study，判断这个 benchmark 是否真的测到了公开基准没覆盖的东西。如果你关心如何把评测反哺训练，重点留意 review 维度是否足够结构化，能否转成 preference data、process reward 或 regression labels。预计 20–30 分钟能抓住主线；如果要落地到内部评测体系，建议把 judge rubric 和 side-by-side 模板细看一遍。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a mismatch in how coding agents are evaluated. Most benchmarks reduce a run to a single bit: did the task pass or fail. That is often too crude for real product use, where users experience the whole trajectory: whether the agent understood the request, used tools safely, verified its own edits, recovered from mistakes, and communicated honestly. AgentLens makes the full interaction trajectory, rather than only the final state, the primary object of evaluation.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining paper, but it matters for post-training, agent optimization, and behavior diagnosis. As foundation models are increasingly exposed through tool use and multi-step interaction, final success alone hides many useful training signals. The main contribution here is to turn evaluation into something that can support diagnosis, preference collection, and regression monitoring, not just leaderboard ranking. For teams working on coding agents, tool-use SFT, or trajectory-level reward modeling, this is a more realistic target than pass rate alone.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core idea is a trajectory-level evaluation protocol. Each run records the full session: user messages, agent responses, tool calls, file edits, command executions, verification attempts, final answer, and final repository state. Evaluation combines formal verification, when objective checks exist, with LLM-written trajectory reviews and metric-specific scoring. The dimensions include things like instruction following, tool discipline, validation behavior, recovery from errors, and user-facing communication. The important design choice is that the written review is treated as a first-class artifact, not just a hidden judge score. That makes the benchmark useful for diagnosis.

A second key component is side-by-side review. Instead of only scoring one trajectory in isolation, the benchmark also compares two agents or two versions on the same task. This is well suited for model comparison, feature evaluation, and regression analysis, because many product regressions show up as local behavior changes before they show up in final pass rate.

On the task side, AgentLens focuses on production-like interactive coding workflows and uses a simulated user driven by another LLM conditioned on a persona and task objective. This follows the hidden-goal interaction style seen in benchmarks like τ-bench. It allows the benchmark to cover tasks without a natural binary outcome, such as writing documentation or explaining a codebase. The paper also includes reliability and bias checks, which is important because LLM-as-judge setups are otherwise easy to overtrust.
summary_en.experiments: From the provided text, the empirical section includes at least four parts: a leaderboard of current models, qualitative analysis of behavioral differences captured by trajectory reviews, a correlation study against public benchmarks, and a nightly evaluation pipeline used to catch regressions in an actively developed production coding agent. The excerpt does not provide concrete numbers for model rankings, task counts, judge agreement, metric weights, or correlation coefficients, so those should not be inferred. The most important things to verify in the full paper are judge reproducibility, whether pairwise review is more stable than absolute scoring, how formal verification and trajectory review complement each other, and whether the benchmark can detect regressions that pass/fail metrics miss.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim-to-medium-depth read. Focus on the evaluation protocol, not on model details. Start with the introduction to understand why the authors reject single-bit evaluation for coding agents.
