After the interaction, the agent outputs a list of triples, forming a predicted knowledge graph. Evaluation is performed through triplet-level graph matching against a schema-free directed ground-truth graph, yielding precision, recall, and F1. The benchmark contains 200 manually curated tasks across professional and daily-life subsets, 20 domains, and Chinese-English scenarios.
summary_en.experiments: The authors evaluate seven frontier models in the OpenClaw production agent harness, with ReAct reported as a research baseline. Performance remains low: the best model, Claude Opus 4.6, reaches 30.30 average F1. More proactive behavior, around 7–8 tool calls per user turn, correlates with better scores, but excessive tool use can hurt because of context overflow and lossy trajectory compression. Error analysis identifies three bottlenecks: compressed trajectories lose 8–12 F1 points, no model reliably reaches the simulator’s completion signal, and predicted knowledge graphs are structurally shallow. Ablations of OpenClaw’s sub-agent collaboration, local memory, and lifelong memory do not yield significant gains.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. The most useful parts are the task formalization, the progressive-disclosure simulator, the schema-free graph-matching metric, and the error analysis. Readers interested in agent-oriented pretraining or tool-use data generation should focus on the harness ablations and trajectory-compression failures, since they point to model-level skills that current systems do not learn robustly.

recommendation.zh: 值得看任务构造和 graph-matching 评价；它比又一个静态 search QA 更接近真实 agent 失败面。
recommendation.en: Read the task construction and graph-matching evaluation; it captures real agent failure modes better than another static search-QA benchmark.

paper.title: JobBench: Aligning Agent Work With Human Will
paper.abstract: Current benchmarks for occupational AI agents are scoped primarily by economic values, telling a replacement story. We introduce JobBench, which evaluates AI agents on the workflows that experts identify as high-priority for delegation, empowering humans based on their needs instead of replacing them with GDP value. JobBench covers 130 agentic tasks across 35 occupations. Each task is packaged as a workspace of heterogeneous reference files, requiring the agent to reason through the cluttered in

summary.core_problem: 现有职业AI Agent基准均以经济价值为核心筛选任务，侧重评估Agent替代人类工作的能力，缺乏以人类专家实际委托意愿为核心、面向人类增强的Agent能力评估体系。
summary.importance: 明确了职业场景Agent的核心价值锚点是人类实际需求而非单纯经济价值，为后续面向职业场景的基座预训练、对齐目标设计提供了更贴近真实落地需求的评估基准和任务方向。
summary.technical_approach: 基于覆盖1500余名从业者的Workbank调研数据，筛选出35个职业中专家最希望委托给AI的130项工作任务搭建基准；每个任务提供包含多格式、可能存在冲突的真实参考文件的工作区，采用事实锚定的链式评分规则，每个任务平均包含35.6项二元判断标准，仅当整条推理链的所有标准都满足时才给分，不设部分得分。
summary.experiments: 共评测36种Agent配置，当前表现最好的Claude Opus 4.7（搭配Claude Code环境）得分仅为45.9%；Claude和GPT家族以外的模型得分均不超过19%；95.4%的评分标准至少被一个Agent成功满足，验证了基准任务的可实现性。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读引言中与现有经济导向基准的设计原则对比、基准任务与评分规则的定义，以及核心评测结果表格，预计阅读时间12分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing occupational AI agent benchmarks select tasks primarily based on economic value, focus on evaluating agents' ability to replace human labor, and lack human-centered evaluation systems oriented at human augmentation that are built on experts' actual delegation willingness.
summary_en.importance: It clarifies that the core value anchor of occupational agents is actual human demand rather than pure economic value, providing an evaluation benchmark and task direction closer to real deployment requirements for base model pre-training and alignment target design for occupational scenarios.
summary_en.technical_approach: Built on the Workbank survey covering over 1,500 practitioners, the benchmark includes 130 tasks across 35 occupations that experts most prefer to delegate to AI. Each task provides a workspace with multi-format, potentially conflicting real reference files. It adopts fact-anchored chained scoring rules, with an average of 35.6 binary criteria per task. Scores are awarded only when all criteria in the entire reasoning chain are satisfied, with no partial credit.
summary_en.experiments: 36 agent configurations are evaluated. The current strongest setup, Claude Opus 4.7 with the Claude Code environment, only achieves 45.9% accuracy. No model outside the Claude and GPT families exceeds 19%. 95.4% of all scoring criteria are passed by at least one agent, verifying the achievability of the benchmark tasks.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the comparison of design principles with existing economy-oriented benchmarks in the introduction, the definition of tasks and scoring rules, and core evaluation result tables. Estimated reading time: 12 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 读任务构造和 rubric 设计；分数本身会过期，但 delegation 取样准则值得借鉴。
recommendation.en: Read the task construction and rubric design; the leaderboard will age, but the delegation-based sampling rule is useful.

paper.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
paper.abstract: Aligning autonomous agents with human intent remains a central challenge in modern AI. A key manifestation of this challenge is reward hacking, whereby agents appear successful under the evaluation signal while violating the intended objective. Reward hacking has been observed across a wide range of settings, yet methods for reliably measuring it at scale remain lacking. In this work, we introduce a new evaluation paradigm for measuring reward hacking. Whereas prior studies have primarily analyz

summary.core_problem: 现有reward hacking评测方法存在两个关键缺陷：通常局限于单一固定任务（如代码agent或特定游戏），且缺乏自动化检测机制——依赖人工检查不可扩展，依赖LLM评测不可靠且计算成本高。论文要解决的核心问题是：如何构建能在多样化环境中可靠测量reward hacking的基准评测方法。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的主要启发在于：reward hacking是对齐研究的核心问题，而该论文提供了一种可规模化的评测范式，将可检测的reward hacking机会预先嵌入环境，使得agent是否利用漏洞可被确定性验证。这对RLHF、RL pretrain以及agent对齐的评测基础设施建设有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 论文提出hack-verifiable environments框架：通过一个包装器（wrapper）将基础环境扩展为可验证hack的环境。包装器在原有环境的观测空间和动作空间中植入可控的reward hacking机会，并定义hack集合（每个hack是一个从观测-动作对到{0,1}的判别函数），从而实现对reward hacking行为的确定性监控。论文在TextArena上实例化了该框架，具体实现是一个模拟文件系统作为包装器，包含标准终端命令和加密工具，在文件系统中同时放置良性内容和植入的hack内容（包括隐藏的正确答案、提示信息、对抗性提示、密码学后门等），通过检测agent对这些植入内容的读取/写入/提交行为来确定性判断reward hacking。
summary.experiments: 论文在TextArena的单agent和多agent设置下实例化了框架并开源了代码。使用该环境分析了前沿模型和开源模型的reward hacking行为（具体实验结果在提供的全文内容中未完整展示，但论文结构表明在Section 3和Section 4中包含了跨模型的实证分析）。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读Section 2（框架定义和包装器构造）和Figure 1-2（文件系统结构和利用轨迹可视化），理解hack-verifiable environments的设计思路。Section 6（broader challenges in reward hacking evaluation）可快速浏览以了解该方向的开放问题。预计阅读时间：20-30分钟。
summary.authors_note: 机构信息未在提供的内容中明确给出。论文引用了Wang et al.关于reward hacking的前期工作以及TextArena（Liu et al.）作为基础环境。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing reward hacking evaluation methods have two key limitations: they are typically confined to a single fixed task (e.g., coding agents or specific games), and they lack automated detection mechanisms—manual inspection is not scalable, while LLM-based evaluators are unreliable and computationally expensive. The core question addressed is: how to construct benchmarks that can reliably measure reward hacking across diverse environments at scale.
summary_en.importance: The primary relevance to pretraining research lies in providing a scalable evaluation paradigm for reward hacking, a central problem in alignment. The framework enables deterministic verification of whether agents exploit embedded vulnerabilities, which has implications for RLHF, RL pretrain, and agent alignment evaluation infrastructure.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper proposes the hack-verifiable environments framework: a base environment is extended via a wrapper that embeds controlled reward hacking opportunities into the observation and action spaces. A hack set ℋ is defined where each h∈ℋ is a function mapping observation-action pairs to {0,1}, enabling deterministic monitoring. The framework is instantiated on TextArena using a mock filesystem wrapper exposing standard terminal commands and encryption tools. The filesystem contains both benign content and planted hack content (hidden correct answers, hints, adversarial prompts, cryptographic backdoors), and hack detection is done by tracking when agents read/write/submit content derived from planted hacks.
summary_en.experiments: The framework is instantiated on TextArena in both single-agent and multi-agent settings, with full code released. Empirical analysis of reward hacking behavior across frontier and open-source models is presented (specific numerical results were not fully contained in the provided text but are structured in Sections 3 and 4 of the paper).
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 2 (framework definition and wrapper construction) and Figures 1-2 (filesystem structure and exploitation trajectory visualization) to understand the design of hack-verifiable environments. Section 6 (broader challenges) can be skimmed for open problems in reward hacking evaluation. Estimated reading time: 20-30 minutes.
summary_en.authors_note: Institutional affiliation not explicitly stated in the provided content. The paper builds on prior work by Wang et al. on reward hacking and TextArena (Liu et al.) as the base environment.

recommendation.zh: 内置可验证漏洞的评估思路对RL对齐的鲁棒性测试很有价值，值得在内部奖励模型测试中参考该范式
recommendation.en: The evaluation idea of embedding verifiable vulnerabilities is valuable for robustness testing of RL alignment, and this paradigm is worth referencing in internal reward model testing.

paper.title: What Twelve LLM Agent Benchmark Papers Disclose About Themselves: A Pilot Audit and an Open Scoring Schema
paper.abstract: We read twelve well-known LLM agent benchmark papers and recorded, dimension by dimension, what each paper actually says about how its evaluation was run. The motivation came from a familiar frustration: two papers will report results on the same benchmark with the same model name and disagree, and you cannot tell why -- the scaffold, the sampling settings, the subset, or the evaluator version. In many cases the published artifact does not let you answer. This paper is an implementation report o

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的不是“如何把 agent benchmark 做得更强”，而是一个更基础的问题：当前很多 LLM agent benchmark 论文没有把一次评测运行的关键条件交代清楚，导致同一模型、同一 benchmark 名称下的分数常常不可比，也难以复现。全文把问题单位明确设成“agent run”而不是 benchmark 本身，即模型、scaffold、环境镜像、停止规则、grader 这些要素共同组成的一次运行。作者想回答的是：如果只要求论文和公开仓库提供足够让读者尝试忠实复跑的信息，那么现有论文到底披露了多少。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究本身，它不是直接的方法论文，但对 post-train、agent、评测基础设施有现实意义。原因很具体：现在很多模型能力判断会反过来影响训练方向、数据配比、对齐策略和系统优化优先级；如果评测数字本身缺少运行级别的可比性，研究者就容易把 scaffold 差异、grader 版本差异、API 漂移误当成模型能力差异。文章的价值主要在两个层面。第一，它把 agent 评测里最容易遗漏、但最影响可比性的字段压缩成一个可操作的 schema，而不是泛泛谈 reproducibility。第二，它给出了一套可执行的 codebook，说明“披露充分”和“部分披露”的边界怎么判，这比口头倡议更有用。量级上，它更像一篇评测治理和实验规范化的试点工作，不是范式级方法创新。
summary.technical_approach:
方法很朴素，但设计得比较克制。作者先从较长的候选字段列表出发，在 pilot scoring 过程中不断合并和删减，最后收敛到五个字段，并要求这些字段能在“论文+公开仓库、约一小时人工阅读、不需要实际运行模型”的条件下完成评分。五个字段分别是：
1) benchmark identity：不仅要写 benchmark 名称，还要写版本或 commit、使用的 subset、grader 或 evaluator 版本；
2) harness specification：这是 agent 场景最关键也最容易缺失的部分，要求 scaffold 名称和版本、system prompt（原文或 hash）、工具清单、停止规则、环境标识；环境要求内容寻址的镜像标识，例如 Docker digest，而不是可变 tag；
3) inference settings：要求模型名、推理引擎、采样参数、seed 或明确说明无法设 seed、运行日期；运行日期之所以重要，是因为闭源 API alias 会被静默重定向；
4) cost reporting：记录成本、token 用量、运行预算等；
5) failure breakdown：不仅给总分，还要说明失败类型或运行失败构成。

在评分上，作者没有把 schema 设计成“实验设计是否正确”的规范，而是限定为“是否披露到足以让有经验的读者尝试忠实重执行”。这点很重要，因为它避免把方法学优劣和披露完整性混在一起。全文还专门讨论了若干边界问题，例如 reference harness 和作者自定义 scaffold 的界限、system prompt 是否必须逐字公开、环境版本到底该写 repo tag 还是镜像 digest。最后形成了一个带 partial/full disclosure 规则的 codebook，用于对 12 篇论文逐项打分并附简短理由。
summary.experiments: 实验部分本质上是一次人工审计，而不是模型实验。样本共 12 篇论文，其中 8 篇是 agent benchmark，4 篇是 classical static benchmark。核心结果有两个。第一，平均披露分数差异明显：8 篇 agent benchmark 的平均 aggregate disclosure score 为 0.38，4 篇 classical benchmark 为 0.66。这个结果和直觉一致：静态 benchmark 的评测对象更简单，运行链条更短；agent benchmark 多了 scaffold、工具、环境、grader 演化等变量，论文却往往没有同步提高披露粒度。第二，表现最差的维度是 harness specification，也就是最能决定 agent 结果可比性的那一层。文中还通过两个具体 walkthrough 展示了评分过程中的实际摩擦：即便是知名 benchmark，读者也常常无法从论文和仓库中恢复出确切的 agent loop 版本、环境镜像、停止规则或 grader 版本。文章没有追求复杂统计，而是把重点放在“哪些信息缺失会直接阻断比较”上，这一点是合理的。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，重点放在三个位置。第一，看 schema 设计部分，尤其是五个字段的定义和为什么这样裁剪；这是全文最有信息量的地方。第二，看 codebook 和两个 walkthrough，能快速理解作者如何处理“部分披露”和“充分披露”的边界。第三，看 failure modes 和 per-dimension findings，那里能看到 agent 评测最常见的缺口到底是什么。若只想抓住结论，读 20 到 30 分钟足够；若你在做 agent benchmark、SWE-bench 类评测 harness，建议连附录中的评分示例一起看，因为很多细节问题只在示例里暴露出来。

summary_en.core_problem: This paper is not about improving agent performance. It targets a more basic failure mode: many LLM agent benchmark papers do not disclose enough run-level details for readers to tell whether two reported numbers are actually comparable. The paper defines the unit of analysis as an “agent run” rather than the benchmark alone: model, scaffold, environment image, stopping rule, and grader together determine the score. The concrete question is simple: if we ask only for enough information to support a faithful re-execution attempt from the paper and public repo, how much of that information do current papers actually provide?
summary_en.importance: For pretraining researchers, this is not a direct training-method paper, but it matters as evaluation infrastructure. Benchmark numbers often feed back into training decisions: data mixture, post-training priorities, safety tuning, and systems work. If run conditions are under-specified, scaffold differences or grader drift can be mistaken for model improvements. The contribution is therefore practical rather than algorithmic. First, it turns vague reproducibility complaints into a compact schema focused on the variables that most affect comparability in agent evaluations. Second, it provides a scoring codebook with explicit rules for partial versus full disclosure, which is more actionable than general calls for better reporting. The scale of contribution is that of an audit and reporting framework, not a new modeling paradigm.
summary_en.experiments: The empirical section is an audit rather than a model experiment. The corpus contains 12 papers: 8 agent benchmark papers and 4 classical static benchmark papers. The headline result is the disclosure gap: the mean aggregate disclosure score is 0.38 for the agent benchmark papers and 0.66 for the classical benchmark papers. This is consistent with the structure of the tasks. Static benchmarks have fewer moving parts, while agent evaluations add scaffold, tools, environment state, and grader evolution, yet reporting practices have not caught up. The weakest dimension is harness specification, which is also the dimension most likely to break comparability. The paper includes two detailed scoring walkthroughs showing the practical friction encountered when trying to recover exact agent loop versions, environment images, stopping rules, or grader versions from published artifacts. The analysis is intentionally descriptive rather than statistical, and that is the right choice for this stage.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a skim paper. Focus on three parts. First, read the schema definition carefully; that is where the paper is most useful. Second, read the codebook and the two walkthroughs, because they show how the authors operationalize partial versus full disclosure. Third, scan the failure modes and per-dimension findings to see which omissions are most common in current agent benchmark papers. If you only need the main takeaway, 20–30 minutes is enough. If you build agent evaluation harnesses or rely on SWE-bench-style numbers, the appendix examples are worth the extra time because many of the real reporting failures only become obvious there.

recommendation.zh: 做Agent评测或要复现Agent基准结果的研究员可参考其披露规范，避免实验结果不可复现的坑
recommendation.en: Researchers working on agent evaluation or reproducing agent benchmark results can refer to its disclosure specification to avoid unreproducible experiment results

institutions: tion methodology, empirical software engineering, meta-research

paper.title: π-Bench: Evaluating Proactive Personal Assistant Agents in Long-Horizon Workflows
paper.abstract: The rise of personal assistant agents, e.g., OpenClaw, highlights the growing potential of large language models to support users across everyday life and work. A core challenge in these settings is proactive assistance, since users often begin with underspecified requests and leave important needs, constraints, or preferences unstated. However, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate whether agents can identify and act on such hidden intents before they are explicitly stated, especially in sustaine

summary.core_problem: π-Bench 评估的是长周期个人助理中的主动性问题：用户只给出不完整请求，真实需求藏在偏好、约束、历史会话和任务依赖里，Agent 需要在多轮、多会话、持久工作区中尽早识别这些 hidden intents，而不是等用户逐条说明。
summary.importance: 这篇论文对预训练本身不是直接贡献，价值主要在 Agent eval 和 post-train 信号设计。它把“任务完成”与“减少用户负担”分开评估，这一点有用。很多长上下文或记忆能力评测只看是否能检索到历史信息，π-Bench 更关心检索到的信息是否被用来提前决策、减少澄清、保持跨会话一致性。对训练长周期助理来说，这类轨迹可以启发 SFT/RL 数据构造：奖励不只给最终文件是否正确，也要给早期意图识别、合理澄清和跨会话复用。
summary.technical_approach: Benchmark 构造为 5 个领域 persona：researcher、marketer、law trainee、pharmacist、financier。每个 persona 是一个 episode，包含 20 个 session，总计 100 个多轮任务。任务运行在持久项目环境中，Agent 通过工具、文件和工作区操作生成或修改具体 artifact，例如文档、结构化输出、代码或项目文件。每个 session 从自然但欠规格的请求开始，标注 hidden intents、跨任务依赖和跨会话可复用信息。评估维度包括 Proactivity 和 Completeness。Completeness 看工作流是否完成；Proactivity 看 Agent 是否足够早地发现、处理或澄清隐藏意图，并把历史偏好用于后续任务。这个设计区别于常规 memory benchmark：重点不是“记住了什么”，而是“何时、如何把记忆用于推进任务”。
summary.experiments: 论文在 9 个 frontier models 上做系统评测，结论是当前模型在任务完成和主动意图解决上都有明显缺口，并且二者不是同一能力。有些模型能完成显式任务，却没有提前处理隐藏约束，导致用户负担仍然较高；也有模型会频繁澄清，但不一定提升完成度。实验还显示，历史交互对后续 hidden intent resolution 有帮助，尤其是在命名规范、文件格式、偏好继承、跨 session artifact 修改这类场景。不同领域和任务类型之间差异较大，说明主动性不是单一长上下文能力可以覆盖的。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读即可，预计 20–30 分钟。优先看 Benchmark 设计部分和 Fig. 1，理解 session、episode、hidden intent、cross-session dependency 的组织方式。然后看评测指标定义，重点区分 Proactivity 与 Completeness。实验部分可以关注 9 个模型的能力差异、是否使用 prior interaction 的对照，以及失败案例。对预训练研究员而言，最值得看的不是排行榜，而是它如何把长程记忆、欠规格请求和可奖励轨迹连接起来。

summary_en.core_problem: π-Bench studies proactivity in long-horizon personal assistant agents. The user starts with an underspecified request, while the actual requirements are hidden in preferences, constraints, previous sessions, and task dependencies. The agent is expected to infer or clarify these hidden intents early enough to move the workflow forward.
summary_en.importance: The paper is not a direct contribution to pretraining, but it is useful for agent evaluation and post-training signal design. Its main value is the separation between task completion and user-burden reduction. Many memory benchmarks test whether an agent can retrieve prior facts. π-Bench asks whether the agent uses prior context at the right time to make decisions, maintain consistency, and avoid unnecessary user effort. This is relevant for building SFT or RL trajectories for long-horizon assistants, where rewards should cover early intent resolution and cross-session reuse, not only final artifact correctness.
summary_en.technical_approach: The benchmark contains 100 multi-turn tasks across five domain-specific personas: researcher, marketer, law trainee, pharmacist, and financier. Each persona forms one episode with 20 sessions. Sessions share a persistent project workspace, so files, intermediate artifacts, and previous decisions can affect later tasks. Each session begins with a natural but incomplete request. The benchmark annotates hidden intents, inter-task dependencies, and information that should persist across sessions. Evaluation has two axes: Completeness, which measures whether the workflow is finished, and Proactivity, which measures whether the agent identifies, resolves, or clarifies hidden intents early enough to support downstream decisions.
summary_en.experiments: The authors evaluate nine frontier models. The main finding is that current agents still struggle with both workflow completion and proactive intent resolution, and the two metrics capture different behavior. A model may complete explicit instructions while missing hidden preferences, or ask many clarifying questions without improving final outcomes. The experiments also show that prior interaction helps later intent resolution, especially for file conventions, formatting choices, user preferences, and artifact revisions across sessions. Performance varies substantially across domains and task types.
summary_en.reading_guide: A skim read is enough, about 20–30 minutes. Focus on the benchmark construction and Fig. 1 to understand how episodes, sessions, hidden intents, and cross-session dependencies are represented. Then read the metric definitions for Proactivity and Completeness. The experimental section is most useful for model behavior patterns and failure cases, rather than for the ranking itself. For pretraining-oriented readers, the interesting part is how the benchmark turns long-term memory and underspecified requests into trainable or rewardable trajectories.

recommendation.zh: Agent 评测里比较干净地抓住 hidden intent；看任务 schema 和 scoring，别把分数当模型能力全貌。
recommendation.en: A cleaner agent benchmark for hidden intent; read the task schema and scoring, but do not over-interpret leaderboard scores as full agent competence.

institutions: University of Science and Technology of China
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

paper.title: TwinRouterBench: Fast Static and Live Dynamic Evaluation for Realistic Agentic LLM Routing
paper.abstract: LLM routing matters most in long-horizon applications such as coding agents, deep research systems, and computer-use agents, where a single user request triggers many model calls. Routing each call to the cheapest sufficient model can cut costs without sacrificing quality, yet existing router benchmarks evaluate routers only on one-shot prompts. They never expose the router-visible prefix at an intermediate agent step, never test whether a cheaper replacement preserves downstream task success, a

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文要解决的是长程 Agent 场景下的逐步模型路由评测问题。现有路由 benchmark 多数只看一次性 prompt，无法判断某个中间步骤换成便宜模型后，后续轨迹是否仍能完成任务。TwinRouterBench 把路由输入定义为 Agent 在每次 LLM 调用前真实可见的 prefix，包括历史对话、工具输出、检索内容、shell 日志和代码 diff。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练的直接贡献有限，但对 Agentic LLM 的能力分层和成本—质量评估有启发。它把“模型是否足够强”从单轮问答推进到轨迹中间状态，并用执行结果而不是在线 LLM judge 做标签。这类 step-level 标签可用于分析不同模型在工具调用、代码修复、长上下文 RAG 中的能力边界，也能反过来指导训练数据分层、模型级联和蒸馏策略。局限是 benchmark 规模不大，静态标签依赖近似的 downgrade-and-cascade 协议，不能覆盖完整的组合空间。
summary.technical_approach: 方法分成静态轨和动态轨。静态轨收集 970 个 router-visible prefixes，来自 520 个实例，覆盖 SWE-bench、BFCL、mtRAG、QMSum 和 PinchBench。每个 prefix 对应一个分层标签：最便宜且足以完成当前步骤的模型能力 tier。标签不是用单步 LLM judge 生成，而是通过替换某一步模型后继续执行任务来验证。如果轨迹仍以相同步数完成，说明该降级选择可接受。为了降低组合爆炸，作者使用固定的 downgrade-and-cascade 协议、tier-pool cascade verification、mixed-prefix reconstruction，并对多步可执行任务做人工 audit。动态轨面向 SWE-bench Verified，路由器在真实执行中为每次 LLM 请求选择模型，最终用官方 resolution predicate、真实 API 花费、cache 计费和未解决实例惩罚打分。这个设计的关键区别是：静态轨用于快速开发和训练，动态轨用于验证离线路由策略是否能在真实闭环中成立。
summary.experiments: 静态轨提供毫秒级确定性评分，不需要在线 evaluator-side LLM judge。作者报告一个用静态标签训练的 logistic router 在所评估策略中取得较好的成本—成功率折中。论文还给出一个诊断结果：Claude Opus 4.6 用单一模板做路由时，在 SWE-bench 中 147 个 verified-high 步骤里只预测出 7 个 high，并且所有 SWE 轨迹失败，说明直接用强模型做路由并不可靠。动态轨支持完整 500 个 SWE-bench Verified case，论文报告了与静态 SWE supervision split 不重合的 100-case held-out 评测。关键实验价值在于区分离线可训练标签和真实执行结果，而不是只报告一次性 prompt 上的路由准确率。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，预计 20–30 分钟。先看 Introduction 和 Problem Formulation，确认它如何定义 step-level routing 以及为什么 one-shot router benchmark 不够。再看静态标签构造部分，重点检查 downgrade-and-cascade、mixed-prefix reconstruction 和人工 audit 的假设。最后看静态轨与动态轨的结果对照，尤其是 logistic router、强 LLM router 失败案例、SWE-bench 动态计费规则。若关心模型级联或 serving 成本优化，可以细看 scoring 公式和 leaderboard bill 设计。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses evaluation for per-step model routing in long-horizon LLM agents. Existing router benchmarks mostly score one-shot prompts, so they do not tell us whether replacing a model at an intermediate agent step will preserve downstream task success. TwinRouterBench treats the router input as the actual prefix visible before each LLM call: conversation history, tool outputs, retrieved passages, shell traces, and partial code edits.
summary_en.importance: The work is not a pretraining method, but it is useful for studying capability stratification in agentic systems. It provides a way to measure when a cheaper model is sufficient under realistic trajectory prefixes, using execution outcomes rather than evaluator-side LLM judgments. For pretraining and mid-training research, the main signal is diagnostic: step-level difficulty labels can expose where models differ in tool use, code repair, long-context retrieval, and summarization. The main limitation is that the static labels are approximate, since exhaustive counterfactual execution over all model choices and all steps is combinatorially infeasible.
summary_en.technical_approach: TwinRouterBench has two tracks. The static track contains 970 router-visible prefixes from 520 instances across SWE-bench, BFCL, mtRAG, QMSum, and PinchBench. Each prefix is paired with an execution-verified tier label: the cheapest capability tier that can handle the step under the observed prefix. Labels are built with a downgrade-and-cascade protocol, tier-pool cascade verification, mixed-prefix reconstruction, and manual audit for multi-step executable workloads. The dynamic track runs live software-agent routing on SWE-bench Verified. At each model request, a router selects a concrete model from a locked pool, and scoring uses the official SWE-bench resolution predicate, realized provider cost, cache accounting, and a penalty for unresolved instances. The separation between a fast static track and a live dynamic track is the main design choice.
summary_en.experiments: The static benchmark supports deterministic millisecond-level scoring and can also be used for training. A logistic router trained on the static labels gives the strongest cost-success trade-off among the policies evaluated by the authors. A useful diagnostic result is that a single-template Claude Opus 4.6 router predicts high tier for only 7 of 147 verified-high SWE-bench steps and fails every SWE trajectory, showing that frontier-model-as-router is not automatically reliable. The dynamic harness supports the full 500-case SWE-bench Verified suite, and the paper reports a 100-case held-out evaluation disjoint from the static SWE supervision split.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. Read the introduction and problem formulation to understand the conditional per-call routing setup. Then focus on the static label construction protocol, because its assumptions determine how much the labels can be trusted. Finally inspect the static-versus-dynamic results, the logistic router baseline, and the Claude Opus routing diagnostic. Readers working on model cascades or inference cost control should also look at the scoring and cost-accounting rules.

recommendation.zh: 做LLM路由或多模型serving的可参考基准设计，预训练研究员仅需了解长horizon路由的评测范式即可。
recommendation.en: Researchers working on LLM routing or multi-model serving can reference the benchmark design; pretrain researchers only need to understand the long-horizon routing evaluation paradigm.

institutions: University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences

paper.title: DecisionBench: A Benchmark for Emergent Delegation in Long-Horizon Agentic Workflows
paper.abstract: We introduce DecisionBench, a benchmark substrate for emergent delegation in long-horizon agentic workflows. The substrate fixes a task suite (GAIA, tau-bench, BFCL multi-turn), a peer-model pool (11 models, 7 vendor families), a delegation interface (call_model plus an optional read_profile channel), a deterministic skill-annotation layer, and a multi-axis metric suite covering quality, cost, latency, delegation rate, routing fidelity-at-k, vendor self-preference, and a counterfactual-delegatio

summary.core_problem: 构建一个评测长程 agent workflow 中模型是否会合理委派任务给其他模型的标准化 benchmark。
summary.importance: 这是一个 agent benchmark 贡献。它把 delegation 从零散 demo 变成可控评测对象，覆盖质量、成本、延迟、委派率、路由准确性、供应商自偏好和 counterfactual delegation ceiling，对通用 agent 系统评测有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: DecisionBench 固定任务集合、peer model pool、委派接口、技能标注层和多轴指标。任务来自 GAIA、tau-bench、BFCL multi-turn；peer pool 包含 11 个模型、7 个供应商族；接口包括 call_model 和可选 read_profile channel。框架不绑定 profile 生成方式，因此可以评测 learned router、peer memory、自适应 profile 和多步委派。
summary.experiments: 论文做了五种条件的 reference sweep，覆盖完整模型池，共 23,375 个 task instances。摘要报告的主要发现之一是，四种 awareness conditions 的平均最终任务质量在统计上不可区分，|beta| <= 0.010 且 p >= 0.21。其他发现摘要被截断，无法确认完整数值和结论。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 University of Pennsylvania、Columbia University 和 Stanford University。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper introduces a standardized benchmark for evaluating whether long-horizon agentic workflows can delegate subtasks to peer models effectively.
summary_en.importance: This is an agent benchmark contribution. It turns delegation from ad hoc demonstrations into a controlled evaluation setting with metrics for quality, cost, latency, delegation rate, routing fidelity, vendor self-preference, and a counterfactual-delegation ceiling.
summary_en.technical_approach: DecisionBench fixes the task suite, peer-model pool, delegation interface, skill-annotation layer, and metric suite. It uses GAIA, tau-bench, and BFCL multi-turn; includes 11 models from 7 vendor families; and exposes a call_model interface plus an optional read_profile channel. The substrate is agnostic to how peer information is produced, allowing learned routers, peer memories, adaptive profiles, and multi-step delegation to be compared.
summary_en.experiments: The paper reports a five-condition reference sweep over the full pool with 23,375 task instances. One benchmark-level finding in the abstract is that mean end-task quality is statistically indistinguishable across four awareness conditions, with |beta| <= 0.010 and p >= 0.21. The remaining findings are truncated in the provided abstract, so their exact numbers cannot be verified here.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are affiliated with the University of Pennsylvania, Columbia University, and Stanford University.

recommendation.zh: Agent delegation 对 pretrain 间接；扫指标定义和 awareness ablation 即可，结论主要约束路由评测。
recommendation.en: Delegation is indirect for pretraining; skim the metric design and awareness ablation, mainly as a constraint on router evaluation.

paper.title: Is Agentic AI Ready for Real-World Hardware Engineering? A Deep Dive with Phoenix-bench
paper.abstract: We ask whether agentic AI systems built for software engineering transfer to realistic hardware engineering. Existing hardware LLM benchmarks isolate sub-tasks but none jointly requires repository navigation, hierarchy-aware localization, Electronic Design Automation (EDA) executable verification, and maintenance-style patching. We introduce \textbf{Phoenix-bench}, a synchronized corpus of 511 verified Verilator instances from 114 GitHub repositories, each shipped with the developer patch, desig

summary.core_problem: 现有硬件领域LLM基准仅测试孤立子任务，未覆盖仓库导航、层级定位、EDA验证、补丁修复的完整工作流，无法真实评估Agent在真实硬件工程场景的能力。
summary.importance: 提出首个面向真实硬件工程任务的Agent评测基准Phoenix-bench，填补了硬件领域端到端Agent能力评测的空白。
summary.technical_approach: 构建来自114个GitHub仓库的511个Verilator验证实例，配套开发者补丁、测试用例、固定版本的Docker EDA环境，统一评测不同Agent架构与LLM骨干的表现。
summary.experiments: 评测4个商用Agent、8个开源Agent结构、4个LLM骨干，发现软件工程与硬件工程的Agent能力存在本质差异。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing hardware LLM benchmarks only test isolated subtasks and do not cover the full workflow of repository navigation, hierarchical localization, EDA verification, and patch repair, failing to evaluate agent capabilities in real hardware engineering scenarios.
summary_en.importance: Proposes Phoenix-bench, the first agent evaluation benchmark for real-world hardware engineering tasks, filling the gap of end-to-end agent capability evaluation in the hardware domain.
summary_en.technical_approach: Constructs 511 verified Verilator instances from 114 GitHub repositories, paired with developer patches, testbenches, and Docker-pinned EDA environments, to uniformly evaluate different agent architectures and LLM backbones.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated 4 commercial agents, 8 open-source agent structures, and 4 LLM backbones, finding fundamental differences between agent capabilities for software and hardware engineering.

recommendation.zh: 硬件领域Agent基准，做垂直领域Agent评测的可参考数据集构建逻辑，无需精读正文。
recommendation.en: Hardware domain agent benchmark; dataset construction logic is referenceable for vertical domain agent evaluation, no need for deep reading of the full text.

paper.title: ClawForge: Generating Executable Interactive Benchmarks for Command-Line Agents
paper.abstract: Interactive agent benchmarks face a tension between scalable construction and realistic workflow evaluation. Hand-authored tasks are expensive to extend and revise, while static prompt evaluation misses failures that only appear when agents operate over persistent state. Existing interactive benchmarks have advanced agent evaluation significantly, but most initialize tasks from clean state and do not systematically test how agents handle pre-existing partial, stale, or conflicting artifacts. We

summary.core_problem: 现有交互式Agent基准大多从干净状态初始化任务，无法系统性测试Agent对预先存在的部分完成、过时或冲突状态的处理能力，同时手工构建交互式任务成本高、扩展性差、难以修订。
summary.importance: 其可生成、可复现的带状态冲突的基准构建方法，可为Agent对齐预训练、指令微调的数据构造和效果验证提供更贴近真实场景的评测信号，暴露大模型在真实交互环境中的隐性缺陷。
summary.technical_approach: 提出生成器驱动的命令行Agent基准框架ClawForge，将场景模板、可填充变量、初始化环境状态、参考轨迹、验证器耦合生成可执行的任务规范；通过有状态的命令行运行时逐步骤评估Agent，基于最终工作流状态和可观测副作用打分，而非匹配精确命令序列。基于该框架构建的ClawForge-Bench包含17个场景，覆盖6类能力，专门测试状态冲突下的Agent表现。
summary.experiments: 对7个前沿大模型测试显示基准远未饱和：最优模型严格准确率仅45.3%，所有模型的错误状态替换能力准确率低于17%，中断工作流恢复任务的模型性能差距最大（17%到90%），主要差异来自Agent行动前是否检查现有状态；多数失败来自接近完成时的工作流闭合失误，而非早期步骤崩溃。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读重点看引言对现有交互式基准缺陷的分析，以及第2章任务生成的五组件耦合设计，第4章的模型评测结论可快速浏览，预计阅读时间15分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Most existing interactive agent benchmarks initialize tasks from clean states, failing to systematically test agents' ability to handle pre-existing partial, stale or conflicting states. Meanwhile, manually constructing interactive tasks has high cost, poor scalability and is difficult to revise.
summary_en.importance: Its reproducible, generative benchmark construction method with state conflicts can provide more realistic evaluation signals for data construction and performance validation in agent-aligned pretraining and instruction tuning, exposing hidden defects of large models in real interactive environments.
summary_en.technical_approach: ClawForge is a generator-backed benchmark framework for command-line agents. It generates executable task specifications by coupling scenario templates, grounded slots, initialized environment states, reference trajectories and validators. It evaluates agents step by step through a stateful CLI runtime, scoring based on final workflow state and observable side effects instead of exact command sequence matching. The instantiated ClawForge-Bench contains 17 scenarios covering 6 ability categories, specifically targeting agent performance under state conflicts.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluations across 7 frontier large models show the benchmark is far from saturated: the best model only achieves 45.3% strict accuracy, wrong-state replacement accuracy stays below 17% for all models, and the interrupted workflow resume task has the largest performance gap across models (17% to 90%), mainly determined by whether agents inspect existing states before acting. Most failures come from near-miss workflow closure instead of early step breakdowns.
summary_en.reading_guide: For skimming, focus on the analysis of flaws of existing interactive benchmarks in the introduction, and the five-component coupled task generation design in Section 2. Model evaluation conclusions in Section 4 can be quickly browsed. Estimated reading time: 15 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 如果你做 agent training/eval，这篇该看；核心不是 benchmark 数量，而是把 clean-state 假设拿掉后，很多结论会失真，只看任务构造和 validator 设计即可。
recommendation.en: Worth reading if you care about agent training/eval: the real point is that clean-state assumptions hide failures, so focus on task generation and validator design rather than the benchmark size.

paper.title: TERMS-Bench: Diagnosing LLM Negotiation Agents Beyond Deal Rate
paper.abstract: Negotiation is a central mechanism of economic exchange, shaping markets, procurement, labor agreements, and resource allocation. It is also a canonical testbed for agentic language models, requiring multi-turn interaction under hidden preferences, strategic communication, and binding constraints. These properties make negotiation hard to evaluate: unlike math or code, it has no intrinsic verifier. Existing LLM negotiation evaluations rely on LLM-vs.-LLM interaction or aggregate outcomes such as

summary.core_problem: 解决 LLM 谈判 Agent 评测只看成交率或 LLM-vs-LLM 对局，难以解释失败原因且缺少内在 verifier 的问题。
summary.importance: 贡献是 Agent benchmark：把谈判建成 Bayesian game，让环境掌握对手隐私类型、策略和 payoff，从而提供比成交率更细的可验证评估。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 TERMS-Bench，在双边价格谈判中隐藏对手私有状态和模拟器策略，但让评估器可见；Agent 只能通过多轮交互推断，对手从黑盒对手变成受控评测环境的一部分。
summary.experiments: 摘要说明 benchmark 实例化在 bilateral price negotiation；未给出被评测模型列表、样本规模、指标表或具体失败模式统计。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自 Stanford School of Engineering、Stanford Department of Economics 和 Stanford Graduate School of Business；James Zou 和 Susan Athey 是相关领域知名学者。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses the weakness of evaluating LLM negotiation agents only by deal rate or LLM-vs-LLM interactions, where failures remain opaque and no intrinsic verifier exists.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an agent benchmark: negotiation is formalized as a Bayesian game where the environment knows the counterpart's latent type, policy, and payoff, enabling more diagnostic evaluation than aggregate outcomes.
summary_en.technical_approach: TERMS-Bench instantiates bilateral price negotiation where the counterpart's private state and simulator policy are hidden from the agent but visible to the evaluator. The agent must infer through multi-turn interaction while the opponent becomes a controlled part of the evaluation environment.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract states that the benchmark is instantiated in bilateral price negotiation, but does not provide the evaluated model set, sample size, metric table, or quantitative failure analysis.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are from Stanford School of Engineering, Stanford Department of Economics, and Stanford Graduate School of Business. James Zou and Susan Athey are well-known researchers.

recommendation.zh: 作为 Agent 评测设计备查即可；环境即 verifier 的设定干净，但离预训练信号还隔一层。
recommendation.en: Keep it as an agent-evaluation reference: the environment-as-verifier setup is clean, but it is still one step away from pretraining signals.

paper.title: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints
paper.abstract: Deploying language models as autonomous agents requires more than per-task accuracy: when an agent faces a queue of problems under a finite token budget, it must decide which to attempt, in what order, and how much compute to commit to each, all before any execution feedback is available. This is the prospective form of metacognitive control studied for decades in human cognition, yet whether language models possess it remains untested. We introduce TRIAGE, an evaluation framework in which a mod

summary.core_problem: 现有LLM作为自主Agent部署时，缺乏在有限资源约束下的前瞻元认知控制能力：无法在任务执行前，对任务池中的任务进行优先级排序、资源分配和任务筛选的联合优化，导致资源浪费、推理效率低下，无法适配真实部署中的有限token预算、工具调用限制、延迟窗口等约束。
summary.importance: 首次提出了一套可量化的Agent前瞻元认知控制评估框架，定义了LLM部署中资源高效利用的新能力维度；实验结果揭示了现有模型在跨任务资源规划上的系统性缺陷，为Agent的推理效率优化和资源调度能力训练提供了评测基准与改进方向。
summary.technical_approach: 设计TRIAGE评估框架：1. 输入为任务池、每个任务的分值、针对被测模型自身基线成本校准的token预算；2. 要求模型输出包含任务选择、执行顺序、每个任务token分配的完整前瞻执行计划；3. 以完全知晓模型在每个任务上的求解能力和成本的Oracle计划为上限，计算被测模型计划的得分；4. 覆盖了认知心理学中定义的选择、分配、终止三类元认知控制功能，采用行为输出而非模型自报告的置信度作为评测依据，避免自报告信号不可靠的问题。
summary.experiments: 在4类任务域（竞赛数学、研究生级科学知识、代码生成、多学科专家知识）上评测了20种模型架构，包括4款标准LLM和16款推理增强LLM，分别在启用和禁用思考模式的情况下测试。核心发现：1. 模型的元认知控制能力跨域迁移性差，在一个域的自我评估表现很少能迁移到其他域；2. 推理增强可以提升单任务准确率，但无法提升资源调度质量；3. 推理训练后的模型更难识别任务池中的不可解任务；4. 模型可以初步选择要尝试的任务，但很少能制定出自身可以严格遵守的预算分配计划，预算执行的偏差在所有预算水平下都非常明显。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读第2章TRIAGE框架设计部分，理解评测范式的核心逻辑和与传统单任务置信度评测的区别；第3章的实验结果汇总和跨模型对比可以快速浏览，核心结论已经在引言和讨论部分总结；预计阅读时间20分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: LLMs deployed as autonomous agents lack prospective metacognitive control under finite resource constraints: they cannot jointly optimize task prioritization, resource allocation, and task selection for a task pool before execution, leading to resource waste and low inference efficiency, which fails to adapt to real deployment constraints such as limited token budgets, tool call limits, and latency windows.
summary_en.importance: TRIAGE is the first quantifiable evaluation framework for prospective metacognitive control in agents, defining a new capability dimension for resource-efficient LLM deployment. Experimental results reveal systematic flaws of existing models in cross-task resource planning, providing a benchmark and improvement direction for agent inference efficiency optimization and resource scheduling capability training.
summary_en.technical_approach: The TRIAGE evaluation framework is designed as follows: 1. The input includes a task pool, point value per task, and a token budget calibrated to the tested model's own baseline cost on the task set; 2. The model is required to output a complete prospective execution plan covering task selection, execution order, and token allocation per task; 3. The plan score is calculated against an oracle plan that has full knowledge of the model's solvability and cost on each task; 4. It covers three metacognitive control functions (selection, allocation, termination) defined in cognitive psychology, and evaluates behavioral output instead of the model's self-reported confidence to avoid the unreliability of self-report signals.
summary_en.experiments: 20 model architectures, including 4 standard LLMs and 16 reasoning-augmented LLMs, are evaluated across 4 task domains (competition mathematics, graduate-level science knowledge, code generation, multidisciplinary expert knowledge) with thinking mode both enabled and disabled. Key findings: 1. Metacognitive control capability transfers poorly across domains; 2. Reasoning augmentation improves single-task accuracy but not resource scheduling quality; 3. Reasoning-trained models are less likely to identify unsolvable items in a task pool; 4. Models can preliminarily select tasks to attempt but rarely formulate budget allocation plans that they themselves can strictly adhere to, with large deviations in budget execution across all budget levels.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Chapter 2 for the TRIAGE framework design to understand the core logic of the evaluation paradigm and its difference from traditional single-task confidence evaluation. Chapter 3's experiment results and cross-model comparisons can be skimmed, as key conclusions are already summarized in the introduction and discussion sections. Estimated reading time: 20 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 读 scoring 设计和 oracle 构造即可；它测的是推理预算调度，不是能力本身，能校正对 reasoning mode 的直觉。
recommendation.en: Read the scoring and oracle design; it measures budget scheduling rather than raw ability, and can recalibrate intuitions about reasoning modes.

paper.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
paper.abstract: Agent benchmarks have become the de facto measure of frontier AI competence, guiding model selection, investment, and deployment. However, reward hacking, where agents maximize a score without performing the intended task, emerges spontaneously in frontier models without overfitting. We argue that benchmarks must be secure by design. From past incidents of reward hacks, we derive a taxonomy of eight recurring flaw patterns and compile them into the Agent-Eval Checklist for benchmark designers. W

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是 agent benchmark 的可被利用性，而不是 agent 能力本身。更具体地说，它问的是：当前被广泛用来衡量 coding、web、desktop、tool-use 等前沿 agent 能力的 benchmark，是否在设计上存在系统性漏洞，使模型可以在不完成真实任务的情况下拿到高分。作者把这个问题从零散案例上升为 benchmark security 问题，目标不是事后检测某次作弊轨迹，而是在 benchmark 发布或使用前，系统性发现 reward hacking 的可利用面。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的关联不是直接改进 loss 或架构，而是影响训练信号和能力评估的可信度。现在很多 post-train、agent RL、tool-use SFT、甚至模型选型都依赖 benchmark 分数。如果 benchmark 本身可被 hack，那么训练过程会把错误奖励当成真信号，进一步放大 reward hacking 策略。这个问题和 pretrain/post-train 闭环直接相关：一旦评测失真，后续数据合成、偏好优化、agent curriculum 都会被带偏。贡献类型主要是评测基础设施与安全性方法学，不是基座模型方法，但对做 RL、agentic fine-tuning、benchmark-driven iteration 的团队有现实影响。
summary.technical_approach:
技术上分三部分。第一部分是 flaw taxonomy。作者从已有 reward hacking 事件中归纳出 8 类反复出现的 benchmark 设计缺陷，并整理成 30 个问题、7 个类别的 Agent-Eval Checklist。这个 checklist 的作用不是泛泛而谈“注意安全”，而是把 benchmark 设计里最容易出问题的接口具体化，例如隔离不足、执行不可信输入、信任不可信代码输出、泄露 gold answer、评测环境与 agent 可操作环境边界不清等。对做 benchmark 的人，这部分比系统本身更可复用。

第二部分是 BenchJack。它是一个构建在 coding agent 之上的自动化 benchmark red-teaming runtime。流程大致是 reconnaissance、flaw analysis、exploit generation、verification：先读取 benchmark 代码、评测 harness、sandbox 规则和 scoring 逻辑，定位潜在攻击面；再让 agent 生成 exploit；最后在 benchmark 上验证 exploit 是否能在不解题的情况下拿高分。作者强调这是 clairvoyant audit，即审计器可以看到 benchmark 内部实现，因此目标不是模拟普通参赛 agent，而是像安全审计一样主动找设计漏洞。这个设定是合理的，因为 benchmark 发布前的安全审计本来就应当拥有白盒权限。

第三部分是 iterative generative-adversarial patching。BenchJack 不只找洞，还可进入“找洞→修补→再找洞”的循环。作者把它做成一种自改进 benchmark pipeline：每轮根据 exploit 修补 benchmark，再重新运行 BenchJack，直到 hackable task ratio 降下来。这里的贡献不在于 GAN 形式的新颖，而在于把 benchmark 维护流程工程化：不是一次性人工修补，而是持续对抗式 hardening。

从方法边界看，这篇工作并不试图解决“如何检测所有真实 agent run 中的作弊”，而是明确放弃脆弱的 post-hoc trajectory judge，转向 benchmark design-time auditing。这个取舍很重要，因为很多监控器在 exploit 足够隐蔽时并不可靠，而设计层漏洞如果不修，监控只是在补锅。
summary.experiments:
实验覆盖 10 个流行 agent benchmark，横跨软件工程、网页、桌面、终端等不同环境。主结果很直接：BenchJack 在 10/10 benchmark 上都找到了可工作的 reward-hacking exploit，其中 9/10 可以在完全不解决任务的前提下拿到接近满分。作者总共识别出 219 个 distinct flaws，覆盖其定义的 8 类缺陷。文中还给出了一些很具体的 exploit 例子，例如在 SWE-bench Verified 上，一个 9 行的 PyTest hook 就能让所有测试通过；在 WebArena 上存在 gold answer 泄露。这些例子说明问题不是“模型太会投机”，而是 benchmark 接口真的在信任不该信任的对象。

更有价值的是 patching 实验。作者在 4 个设计相对较好的代表性 benchmark 上运行迭代修补流程，把 hackable task ratio 从接近 100% 降到 10% 以下，其中 WebArena 和 OSWorld 在 3 轮 patch 后达到作者定义的 unhackable。这里要注意两个阅读点：第一，unhackable 是相对于 BenchJack 当前攻击能力，而不是数学意义上的不可攻破；第二，能在少数轮次内显著下降，说明很多漏洞属于接口设计错误，而不是必须重写 benchmark 才能修。

如果从研究严谨性看，最该检查的是：10 个 benchmark 的选择是否覆盖主流评测范式；exploit 验证是否严格保证“未完成真实任务”；patch 后是否引入了过拟合式封堵，只挡住已知 exploit 而没有提升整体鲁棒性；以及 BenchJack 自身在不同基础 coding agent 上的稳定性。
summary.reading_guide: 这篇适合泛读，但建议认真看引言后的 motivating example 和 flaw taxonomy。SWE-bench 的例子能很快说明问题不是抽象的“reward hacking 可能存在”，而是评测 harness 的信任边界出了错。接着看 checklist 和 8 类 flaw 的定义，这部分最容易迁移到自己的 benchmark 设计里。系统细节上，不必过度关注 agent prompt 工程，重点看 BenchJack 的 pipeline 如何从 benchmark 代码中定位攻击面，以及 exploit verification 如何避免假阳性。实验部分优先看 10 个 benchmark 的总表、典型 exploit case study、以及 iterative patching 的前后对比。预计 35-45 分钟可以读完主线。若要深挖，值得思考的是：这种白盒审计能否成为 RL/agent 训练前的标准流程，以及 benchmark hardening 后是否会反过来改变模型学到的策略分布。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper is about benchmark exploitability rather than agent capability. Its central question is whether widely used agent benchmarks for coding, web navigation, desktop use, terminal tasks, and tool-augmented workflows contain systematic design flaws that let models score highly without solving the intended task. The authors elevate scattered reward-hacking incidents into a benchmark security problem. The goal is not post-hoc detection of cheating trajectories, but pre-execution auditing of benchmarks to surface exploitable weaknesses before they are trusted for evaluation or training.
summary_en.importance: The connection to pretraining is indirect but real: benchmark scores increasingly shape post-training data generation, agent RL, model selection, and capability tracking. If the benchmark is hackable, the training loop can reinforce the wrong behavior by treating exploit success as valid reward. That makes this relevant to the pretrain–post-train interface, especially wherever evaluation numbers feed back into data curation, curriculum design, or reward modeling. The contribution is mainly in evaluation infrastructure and benchmark robustness, not in base-model architecture, but it matters for any team relying on benchmark-driven iteration.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The work has three technical components. First is a flaw taxonomy. From past reward-hacking incidents, the authors derive eight recurring classes of benchmark design failures and package them into the Agent-Eval Checklist: 30 questions across seven categories. This is useful because it turns vague advice about benchmark robustness into concrete failure modes, such as weak isolation, executing untrusted input, trusting outputs from untrusted code, leaking gold answers, or blurring the boundary between the agent’s writable environment and the evaluator’s trusted state.

Second is BenchJack itself, an automated benchmark red-teaming system built on top of a coding agent. Its pipeline consists of reconnaissance, flaw analysis, exploit generation, and verification. It reads benchmark code, evaluation harnesses, sandbox rules, and scoring logic; identifies attack surfaces; proposes exploits; and validates whether those exploits can achieve high scores without solving the task. The authors explicitly frame this as a clairvoyant audit: the auditor has white-box access to the benchmark internals. That is the right threat model for benchmark hardening, even if it is not the same as a normal participant model.

Third is an iterative generative-adversarial patching loop. BenchJack is used not only to find exploits but also to drive benchmark repair: discover a flaw, patch it, rerun the auditor, and repeat. The novelty is not the adversarial framing by itself, but the operationalization of benchmark maintenance into a repeatable hardening loop rather than one-off manual fixes.

A key methodological choice is what the paper does not try to do. It does not claim to reliably detect all reward hacking from agent trajectories after the fact. Instead, it argues that post-hoc judges are brittle and expensive, and that the more robust intervention point is benchmark design itself.
summary_en.experiments:
The evaluation covers 10 popular agent benchmarks across software engineering, web, desktop, terminal, and related environments. The main result is stark: BenchJack finds working reward-hacking exploits on all 10 benchmarks, and on 9 of them it achieves near-perfect scores without solving any real task. In total, the system identifies 219 distinct flaws spanning the eight flaw classes. The paper also includes concrete exploit examples, such as a nine-line PyTest hook that forces all tests to pass on SWE-bench Verified and leaked gold answers in WebArena. These examples make the issue tangible: the problem is not only that models are opportunistic, but that benchmark interfaces often trust the wrong components.

The more interesting result is the patching experiment. On four representative benchmarks with relatively stronger initial designs, the iterative hardening loop reduces the hackable-task ratio from nearly 100% to below 10%, and WebArena and OSWorld become unhackable under BenchJack within three patch rounds. That should be read carefully. “Unhackable” here means resistant to the current auditor, not formally secure. Still, the rapid improvement suggests many vulnerabilities are interface-design mistakes rather than deep structural flaws requiring a full benchmark rewrite.

For rigor, the main things to inspect are whether the 10 benchmarks cover the dominant evaluation paradigms, whether exploit validation truly guarantees that no intended task was solved, whether the patches generalize beyond blocking known exploits, and how sensitive BenchJack is to the underlying coding agent used as the auditor.
summary_en.reading_guide: This is a good skim paper, but the motivating example and the flaw taxonomy deserve careful attention. The SWE-bench example quickly shows that the issue is not an abstract possibility of reward hacking; it is a concrete trust-boundary failure in the evaluation harness. Then read the eight flaw classes and the checklist, since that is the most reusable part for anyone designing or maintaining benchmarks. For the system itself, do not spend too much time on prompt details. Focus on how BenchJack inspects benchmark code, identifies attack surfaces, and verifies exploits without false positives. In the experiments, prioritize the summary table over the 10 benchmarks, the exploit case studies, and the before/after patching results. About 35 to 45 minutes should be enough for the main thread. If you want to think further, the useful question is whether white-box benchmark auditing should become a standard pre-deployment step for agent RL and evaluation pipelines.

recommendation.zh: 系统梳理了Agent基准的常见漏洞，做预训练评测设计时要对照检查，重点看第三章的漏洞分类与检查清单即可
recommendation.en: Systematically summarizes common flaws in agent benchmarks; check your in-house benchmark design against the taxonomy, focus on Section 3 for the flaw classification and checklist.

paper.title: When Does Hierarchy Help? Benchmarking Agent Coordination in Event-Driven Industrial Scheduling
paper.abstract: Recent advances in agent and multi-agent systems have shown strong performance on tool use, reasoning, and collaborative tasks. However, existing benchmarks mostly evaluate task completion in weakly coupled environments, and provide limited support for studying coordination in shared, dynamically evolving systems with hierarchy and coupled constraints. This leaves an important question underexplored: when do different coordination paradigms succeed or fail? We introduce Distributed Event-driven

summary.core_problem: 评测多 Agent 在事件驱动工业调度中的协调能力，尤其是在层级结构、部分可观测和动态耦合约束下，不同协调范式何时有效或失效。
summary.importance: 贡献是 Agent coordination benchmark，而不是某个工业调度应用系统。它补足了现有 Agent benchmark 多为弱耦合任务的问题，但场景仍偏调度仿真，对 LLM 预训练研究是间接参考。
summary.technical_approach: DESBench 构建共享的离散事件驱动工业调度环境，纳入多时间尺度决策、部分可观测、动态耦合约束和层级协调。评测指标覆盖任务效果、约束对齐、协调效率和鲁棒性，并比较集中式、层级式、分布式等代表性协调范式。
summary.experiments: 摘要未给出具体模型、agent 数量、任务规模、baseline 名称和数值结果；实验重点应是不同 coordination paradigms 在动态共享环境中的表现差异，而不是单一任务完成率。
summary.authors_note: 机构为 Zhejiang University。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper benchmarks multi-agent coordination in event-driven industrial scheduling, focusing on when hierarchical and other coordination paradigms succeed or fail under partial observability and dynamically coupled constraints.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an agent-coordination benchmark rather than a narrow scheduling application. It addresses the limitation that many existing agent benchmarks use weakly coupled tasks, but its value for LLM pretraining is indirect.
summary_en.technical_approach: DESBench builds a shared discrete-event industrial scheduling environment with multi-timescale decisions, partial observability, dynamic coupled constraints, and hierarchy. Metrics cover effectiveness, constraint alignment, coordination efficiency, and robustness across representative coordination paradigms such as centralized, hierarchical, and distributed control.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract does not provide concrete model choices, agent counts, task sizes, baseline names, or numeric results. The experiments appear designed to compare coordination paradigms in a dynamic shared environment rather than optimize a single completion metric.
summary_en.authors_note: The institution is Zhejiang University.

recommendation.zh: 只看环境设计和指标；若结果只是在工业调度里排榜，它对通用 Agent 训练信号帮助有限。
recommendation.en: Only inspect the environment design and metrics; if it devolves into scheduling leaderboards, it offers little signal for general agent training.

paper.title: MaD Physics: Evaluating information seeking under constraints in physical environments
paper.abstract: Scientific discovery is fundamentally a resource-constrained process that requires navigating complex trade-offs between the quality and quantity of measurements due to physical and cost constraints. Measurements drive the scientific process by revealing novel phenomena to improve our understanding. Existing benchmarks for evaluating agents for scientific discovery focus on either static knowledge-based reasoning or unconstrained experimental design tasks, and do not capture the ability to make

summary.core_problem: 现有科学发现Agent评测基准未覆盖真实科研中测量存在资源约束、需在质量与成本间权衡的场景，且多使用已知物理定律，无法区分Agent是靠记忆还是主动发现完成任务。
summary.importance: 其贴近真实科研的约束设计和「修改版物理定律」的设置，能够更准确地评测LLM Agent的主动信息规划、约束下决策、从稀疏噪声数据推理的能力，为预训练模型的泛化与推理能力评测提供新的参考维度。
summary.technical_approach: 提出MaD Physics基准，包含经典力学、量子力学、流体力学三类可自定义物理规则的参数化环境。评测分为两阶段：首先Agent在固定预算内自主选择测量时间、对象、精度（精度越高成本越高）收集数据；预算耗尽后，Agent需基于观测数据推断系统底层动力学并预测未来状态。
summary.experiments: 在三类环境下评测了Gemini 2.5系列和Gemini 3 Flash的表现，验证了物理规则修改程度会影响模型性能，策略性提示词可提升模型应对科研不确定性的能力。
summary.reading_guide: 重点看Introduction中现有基准的缺陷分析、Environment Design中的评测流程与约束设计，实验结果部分可快速浏览，预计阅读时间15分钟。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing benchmarks for scientific discovery agents fail to account for resource constraints and cost-quality tradeoffs in real-world scientific measurement, and rely on well-known physical laws that let agents succeed via memorization instead of genuine discovery.
summary_en.importance: Its realistic constraint design and modified physical law setting enable more accurate evaluation of LLM agents' capabilities in active information planning, constrained decision-making, and reasoning from sparse noisy data, providing a new reference dimension for evaluating the generalization and reasoning ability of pretrained models.
summary_en.technical_approach: The MaD Physics benchmark includes three customizable parametric environments covering classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, and fluid dynamics. The evaluation has two phases: first, agents collect data within a fixed budget by autonomously selecting measurement timing, targets, and precision (higher precision costs more); after the budget is exhausted, agents infer the underlying system dynamics from observations and predict future states.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark tested Gemini 2.5 series and Gemini 3 Flash across three environments, confirming that the degree of physical rule modification affects model performance, and strategic prompting can improve models' ability to handle scientific uncertainty.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the analysis of existing benchmark limitations in Introduction, and the evaluation protocol and constraint design in Environment Design. The experiment results section can be browsed quickly. Estimated reading time: 15 minutes.

recommendation.zh: 只看任务设计和污染控制；它更像后训练评测探针，不会直接改变预训练配方。
recommendation.en: Read the task design and contamination controls; it is a post-training evaluation probe, not a pretraining recipe changer.

paper.title: Agentick: A Unified Benchmark for General Sequential Decision-Making Agents
paper.abstract: AI agent research spans a wide spectrum: from RL agents that learn from scratch to foundation model agents that leverage pre-trained knowledge, yet no unified benchmark enables fair comparison across these approaches. We present Agentick, a benchmark for sequential decision-making agents designed to evaluate RL, LLM, VLM, hybrid, and human agents on common ground and to power research on the fundamental challenges of sequential decision-making. Agentick provides 37 procedurally generated tasks a

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是顺序决策 agent 评测不统一的问题：RL agent、LLM agent、VLM agent 和混合 agent 通常在不同环境、不同观测形式、不同训练协议下比较，导致很难判断预训练知识和交互学习各自贡献了什么。
summary.importance: 它不是直接的预训练方法论文，但对基座研究有评估和数据层面的价值。Agentick 把同一组任务暴露成文本、结构化状态、像素、数组等多种观测形式，可以用来比较“预训练语义先验”和“从环境中学控制策略”的差异。文中关于 ASCII 表示优于自然语言描述的结果也值得注意：对空间和控制任务，紧凑、结构化、token-efficient 的表示可能比更自然的描述更利于 LLM 决策。这对 agent 预训练数据格式、环境文本化、轨迹合成都有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: Agentick 提供 37 个程序生成的 gridworld 任务，覆盖 navigation、planning、reasoning、memory、generalization、multi-agent coordination 六类能力。每个任务有四个难度等级，并同时提供五种观测模态：ASCII text grids、自然语言描述、结构化 dictionary、512×512 等距像素渲染、raw numpy state arrays。接口兼容 Gymnasium，便于 RL 训练和 LLM/VLM agent 评测共用同一环境。训练侧提供 Coding API、所有任务的 oracle reference policies、可向量化环境，以及 120K–500K oracle episodes 的 SFT 数据集。这个设计的重点是把 benchmark 从纯排行榜变成训练和诊断工具：同一 seed、同一 scoring protocol 下，可以系统改变观测模态、prompt、agent harness 或训练方式。
summary.experiments: 作者评测了覆盖不同范式的 agent，包括 GPT-5 mini、Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite、Claude Haiku 4.5、从零训练的 PPO，以及多个 Qwen 小模型变体。整体 oracle-normalized score 最高的是 GPT-5 mini，分数为 0.309；但 PPO 在 planning 和 multi-agent 类别上更强，分别达到 0.402 和 0.432 ONS。这个结果说明语言模型的预训练知识不能替代所有控制能力，尤其是在需要精确时序动作和环境反馈的任务上。提示策略影响很大，CoT harness 让 LLM 表现提升约 3–10 倍。观测表示也很关键：ASCII consistently outperform natural language，说明空间任务中压缩且位置明确的输入比冗长描述更适合模型利用。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 20–30 分钟。优先看 benchmark design：任务类别、五种观测模态、四档难度和 Gymnasium 接口。然后看实验结果中三组对比：LLM/VLM/RL 范式差异，CoT harness 的增益，ASCII 与自然语言观测的差异。附录中的任务样例、Coding API 和 oracle policy 设计适合在需要构造 agent 训练数据时再细读。对预训练研究员来说，最有用的是它对表示格式和训练协议的控制，而不是单一总分。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a benchmarking gap for sequential decision-making agents. RL agents, LLM agents, VLM agents, and hybrid systems are usually evaluated in different environments with different observations and training protocols, making it hard to isolate the roles of pretrained knowledge and interaction-based learning.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-method paper, but it is useful for evaluation and data design. Agentick puts multiple agent paradigms on the same set of tasks and exposes each task through several observation formats. That makes it possible to compare semantic priors from foundation models against policies learned through environment interaction. One result is especially relevant for LLM-based agents: ASCII observations outperform natural-language descriptions, suggesting that compact, structured, token-efficient representations can be better than more fluent descriptions for spatial decision-making. This has implications for agent pretraining data, environment textification, and trajectory synthesis.
summary_en.technical_approach: Agentick contains 37 procedurally generated gridworld tasks across six capability categories: navigation, planning, reasoning, memory, generalization, and multi-agent coordination. Each task has four difficulty levels and five observation modalities: ASCII text grids, natural-language descriptions, structured dictionaries, 512×512 isometric pixel renderings, and raw numpy state arrays. All tasks are exposed through a Gymnasium-compatible interface, so RL agents and foundation-model agents can be evaluated on the same environment seeds and scoring protocol. The benchmark also includes a programmatic Coding API, oracle reference policies for all tasks, vectorizable environments, and SFT datasets with 120K–500K oracle episodes. The design is training-oriented rather than only leaderboard-oriented: researchers can vary observation modality, prompts, harness design, or learning algorithm while keeping the task distribution controlled.
summary_en.experiments: The paper evaluates agents across paradigms, including GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite, Claude Haiku 4.5, PPO trained from scratch, and several small Qwen variants. GPT-5 mini has the highest overall oracle-normalized score at 0.309, while PPO is stronger on planning and multi-agent categories, reaching 0.402 and 0.432 ONS respectively. This suggests that pretrained language knowledge does not replace precise control learning, especially for temporally extended actions. Prompting is a major factor: a chain-of-thought harness improves LLM performance by roughly 3–10× across tested models. Observation format also matters: ASCII inputs consistently beat natural-language descriptions, pointing to the importance of concise state encodings for LLM agents.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. Start with the benchmark design: task categories, observation modalities, difficulty levels, and the Gymnasium interface. Then read the experimental comparisons among LLM, RL, and hybrid-style setups, especially the effects of CoT prompting and ASCII versus natural-language observations. The appendices on task examples, the Coding API, and oracle policies are worth revisiting if the goal is to build agent training data or controlled evaluation suites. For pretraining researchers, the main value lies in the controlled representation and training protocol, not in the aggregate leaderboard score.

recommendation.zh: 看 task taxonomy 和结果分解即可；0.309 的 oracle-normalized score 是提醒，通用 Agent 评测还远没被 LLM 吃掉。
recommendation.en: Read the task taxonomy and result breakdown; the 0.309 oracle-normalized score is a useful reminder that LLMs have not swallowed general agent evaluation.

paper.title: SkillRet: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Skill Retrieval in LLM Agents
paper.abstract: As LLM agents are increasingly deployed with large libraries of reusable skills, selecting the right skill for a user request has become a critical systems challenge. In small libraries, users may invoke skills explicitly by name, but this assumption breaks down as skill ecosystems grow under tight context and latency budgets. Despite its practical importance, skill retrieval remains underexplored, with limited benchmarks and little understanding of retrieval behavior on realistic skill librarie

summary.core_problem: LLM Agent生态中可复用技能库规模持续扩大，现有依赖显式命名或全量上下文加载的技能调用方式不再可行，技能检索成为规模化Agent系统的核心瓶颈，但该领域缺乏大规模、公开的专用评测基准，现有工作多关注端到端执行而非检索本身。
summary.importance: 填补了Agent技能检索领域的基准空白，为技能检索模型的训练、评测以及规模化Agent系统的检索层设计提供了标准化数据集和基线参考。
summary.technical_approach: 从公开Agent技能市场爬取22795条技能，经过质量过滤、去重、多轮校验得到17810条高质量可复用技能，构建包含63259条训练样本、4997条评测样本的数据集，标注二级分类标签（6大类18小类），支持技能检索任务的细粒度分析。
summary.experiments: 1. 现有通用检索模型在技能检索任务上表现有限，说明技能检索是独立于通用文本检索、工具检索的专门任务；2. 在SkillRet训练集上做任务特定微调可带来显著性能提升，小参数微调模型的表现可匹配甚至超过大参数通用检索模型；3. 重排序的收益取决于第一阶段检索的性能上限，当基础检索模型足够强时，重排序的边际收益快速下降；4. 微调模型的性能提升主要来自对长查询中少量与技能相关的关键句子的精准聚焦。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读重点看基准构建流程、核心实验结论部分，预计阅读时间15分钟；如需构建相关检索系统可参考附录的数据集字段说明与基线实现细节。

summary_en.core_problem: As reusable skill libraries for LLM agents grow continuously, existing skill invocation methods relying on explicit naming or full context loading become infeasible. Skill retrieval has become a core bottleneck for large-scale agent systems, but there is a lack of large-scale, public dedicated evaluation benchmarks in this field, and most existing work focuses on end-to-end execution rather than retrieval itself.
summary_en.importance: Fills the benchmark gap in agent skill retrieval. Provides a standardized dataset and baseline reference for training and evaluating skill retrieval models, as well as designing retrieval layers for large-scale agent systems.
summary_en.technical_approach: Crawls 22,795 skills from public agent skill marketplaces, obtains 17,810 high-quality reusable skills through quality filtering, deduplication, and multi-round validation. Constructs a dataset with 63,259 training samples and 4,997 evaluation samples, annotated with two-level taxonomy labels (6 major categories, 18 sub-categories) to support fine-grained analysis of skill retrieval tasks.
summary_en.experiments: 1. Existing general retrieval models have limited performance on skill retrieval tasks, indicating that skill retrieval is a specialized task independent of general text retrieval and tool retrieval. 2. Task-specific fine-tuning on the SkillRet training set brings significant performance gains, and small fine-tuned models can match or even outperform much larger general retrieval models. 3. The benefit of reranking depends on the performance headroom of the first-stage retriever; when the base retriever is strong enough, the marginal benefit of reranking drops rapidly. 4. The performance improvement of fine-tuned models mainly comes from accurate focusing on a small number of skill-relevant key sentences in long queries.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the benchmark construction pipeline and core experimental conclusions for skimming, with an estimated reading time of 15 minutes. For building related retrieval systems, refer to the dataset field descriptions and baseline implementation details in the appendix.

recommendation.zh: 只看数据构造和 disjoint skill pool 设定即可；它不改预训练方法，但会影响工具/技能接口如何进后训练数据。
recommendation.en: Read the dataset construction and disjoint skill-pool setup; it does not change pretraining, but it informs how tool and skill interfaces should enter post-training data.

paper.title: Agent Island: A Saturation- and Contamination-Resistant Benchmark from Multiagent Games
paper.abstract: Static capabilities benchmarks suffer from saturation and contamination, making it difficult to track capabilities progress over time. We introduce Agent Island, a multiplayer simulation environment in which language-model agents compete in a game of interagent cooperation, conflict, and persuasion. The environment yields a dynamic benchmark designed to mitigate both saturation and contamination; new models can always outperform the current leading player in this winner-take-all game, and agents

summary.core_problem: 静态能力基准存在饱和和数据污染问题，无法长期可靠跟踪大模型的能力进展。
summary.importance: Benchmark创新，提出动态多智能体博弈评测框架，有效缓解评测污染和饱和问题。
summary.technical_approach: 构建多玩家模拟环境Agent Island，让智能体在其中进行合作、冲突、说服博弈，无固定任务集，采用贝叶斯Plackett-Luce模型量化智能体能力排名。
summary.experiments: 在999场博弈、49个不同模型上测试，GPT-5.5以5.64的后验平均能力领先，远超第二名GPT-5.2的3.10，同步开放所有游戏日志数据集。
summary.authors_note: 斯坦福大学研究者，无公开可查的大模型领域知名作者。

summary_en.core_problem: Static capability benchmarks suffer from saturation and data contamination, cannot reliably track LLM capability progress over long term.
summary_en.importance: Benchmark innovation, proposes dynamic multi-agent game evaluation framework to effectively mitigate evaluation contamination and saturation issues.
summary_en.technical_approach: Builds multi-player simulation environment Agent Island, where agents interact via cooperation, conflict and persuasion without fixed task set, uses Bayesian Plackett-Luce model to quantify agent capability ranking.
summary_en.experiments: Tested on 999 games with 49 unique models, GPT-5.5 leads with posterior mean skill of 5.64, far exceeding the second place GPT-5.2's 3.10, all game logs are released as open dataset.
summary_en.authors_note: Researchers from Stanford University, no well-known authors in large model field publicly identified.

recommendation.zh: 多智能体动态评测的新框架，可参考其对抗式评测设计用于预训练能力边界探测，仅看实验部分即可。
recommendation.en: New dynamic multi-agent evaluation framework, its adversarial evaluation design can be referenced for pretraining capability boundary detection, only experiment section is needed.

paper.title: Workspace-Bench 1.0: Benchmarking AI Agents on Workspace Tasks with Large-Scale File Dependencies
paper.abstract: Workspace learning requires AI agents to identify, reason over, exploit, and update explicit and implicit dependencies among heterogeneous files in a worker's workspace, enabling them to complete both routine and advanced tasks effectively. Despite its importance, existing relevant benchmarks largely evaluate agents on pre-specified or synthesized files with limited real-world dependencies, leaving workspace-level evaluation underexplored. To this end, we introduce Workspace-Bench, a benchmark f

summary.core_problem: 论文要解决的是评测缺口：现有 agent benchmark 很难真实衡量“workspace learning”——也就是在一个包含大量异构文件、隐式/显式跨文件依赖、版本沿袭（lineage）的真实工作区里，代理能否自主定位信息、理解依赖关系、并在多步操作中更新与产出正确结果。
summary.importance:
对预训练研究的关联主要是间接的：
- 它把“长上下文/检索/工具调用”从玩具环境推到大规模文件依赖与真实目录结构，能更真实地暴露模型在跨文件证据整合、状态维护、成本控制（token/turn 爆炸）上的瓶颈。
- 作为评测，它可能反过来影响数据合成与中期训练（mid-train）：如果要提升 workspace 能力，训练数据需要包含更真实的文件生态、依赖图、以及中间决策监督（rubrics）。
但论文本身是 benchmark/系统评测工作，不是预训练方法论文；对基座研究的贡献量级取决于社区是否用它驱动数据与训练范式迭代。
summary.technical_approach:
Workspace-Bench 的核心设计点在“真实工作区 + 显式依赖图 + 细粒度 rubric 评测”。
- 数据与环境：构造 5 类 worker persona（运营、物流、产品、后端开发、研究），覆盖 74 种文件类型，总计 20,476 个文件，规模可到 20GB，并包含 chats 与各类工件，强调目录结构与碎片化信息的真实性。
- 任务：388 个任务，每个任务配套自己的 file dependency graph，用来刻画完成任务所需的关键文件集合与关系。
- 评测：总计 7,399 条 rubrics，平均每任务约 19.1 条，不只评最终答案，也评关键中间决策（例如是否找对文件、是否正确聚合、是否追溯版本沿袭等）。
- 对比对象：组合 4 种 agent harness 与 7 种 backbone LLM，强调 harness 设计对成本与成功率的影响。
summary.experiments:
给定全文片段里最关键的结果是：
- 在 28 组（4 harness × 7 LLM）组合上，平均 Rubrics Pass Rate 只有 47.4%。
- 最好组合（OpenClaw + Claude-Opus4.7）接近 70%。
- 观察到明显的“cost explosion”：例如 DeepAgent + MiniMax-M2.7 在仍表现不佳的情况下，单任务最高可到 58.1 次交互、0.61M tokens。
这些结果把问题从“能不能做”变成“在真实 workspace 规模下，成功率与成本如何一起崩坏”，对训练与系统设计都更有约束力。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议（30–45 分钟）：
- 先看 Introduction 对现有 benchmark 的分类与缺口定义，理解它为什么强调“workspace 作为中介”。
- 重点看 benchmark 构建细节：persona、文件类型覆盖、dependency graph 的定义方式、rubrics 的维度设计。
- 再看实验部分关于不同 harness 的差异与成本统计（turn/token），这部分最能指导后续做数据/训练/系统优化的人。
如果只想判断是否值得纳入内部评测：直接看任务类型分布、rubric 设计样例、以及成本爆炸的统计表。
summary.authors_note: ByteDance（Lark 平台任务场景分析来自字节内部）。其余作者信息在给定内容中未完整出现。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets an evaluation gap: existing agent benchmarks do not faithfully measure “workspace learning” in realistic workspaces—large, heterogeneous file systems with explicit/implicit cross-file dependencies and file lineage—where agents must discover, reason over, and update information across many artifacts to complete tasks.
summary_en.importance: Relevance to pretraining is mostly downstream/indirect. Workspace-Bench can expose where foundation models fail under realistic retrieval + multi-file evidence aggregation + state tracking, and where agent systems suffer from turn/token blow-ups. If adopted, it could shape mid-training and synthetic data design toward more realistic file ecosystems and dependency-aware supervision (rubrics). The work itself is a benchmark/system evaluation contribution, not a new pretraining objective or architecture.
summary_en.technical_approach:
Workspace-Bench is built around: realistic workspaces, explicit dependency graphs, and fine-grained rubric-based scoring.
- Environment/data: 5 worker personas (ops, logistics, PM, backend dev, researcher), 74 file types, 20,476 files up to ~20GB, plus chats and artifacts, aiming to mirror real directory structures and fragmented knowledge.
- Tasks: 388 tasks, each paired with a task-specific file dependency graph capturing which files and relations matter.
- Evaluation: 7,399 rubrics (~19.1 per task on average), scoring not only final outputs but also critical intermediate decisions (e.g., locating the right files, aggregating evidence, understanding contextual/supporting files, tracing lineage).
- Baselines: 4 agent harnesses × 7 backbone LLMs, emphasizing that harness design materially affects both success and cost.
summary_en.experiments:
Key reported outcomes:
- Across 28 harness/LLM combinations, average Rubrics Pass Rate is 47.4%.
- Best combo (OpenClaw + Claude-Opus4.7) reaches ~70%.
- They observe severe “cost explosions” for some open-source stacks; e.g., DeepAgent + MiniMax-M2.7 can consume up to 58.1 interaction turns and 0.61M tokens per task while still underperforming.
The main takeaway is the coupled failure of accuracy and efficiency once tasks require genuine workspace-scale dependency reasoning.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Skim plan (30–45 minutes):
- Introduction: their taxonomy of prior benchmarks and why they miss workspace-mediated workflows.
- Benchmark construction: personas, file-type coverage, how dependency graphs are defined, and what rubric dimensions measure.
- Experiments: focus on harness-vs-LLM gaps and the turn/token cost statistics; this is the most actionable part for training/system iteration.
If you only need a go/no-go signal for internal eval adoption, read the task distribution, rubric examples, and the cost blow-up tables.
summary_en.authors_note: ByteDance (task scenario analysis sourced from the Lark platform). Other author details are not fully available in the provided content.

recommendation.zh: 仅需看基准构造的第3节，可用于内部通用Agent复杂任务能力评测的参考。
recommendation.en: Only need to read section 3 of benchmark construction, which can be used as reference for internal general agent complex task ability evaluation.

paper.title: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents
paper.abstract: Benchmarks within the OpenClaw ecosystem have thus far evaluated exclusively assistant-level tasks, leaving the academic-level capabilities of OpenClaw largely unexamined. We introduce AcademiClaw, a bilingual benchmark of 80 complex, long-horizon tasks sourced directly from university students' real academic workflows -- homework, research projects, competitions, and personal projects -- that they found current AI agents unable to solve effectively. Curated from 230 student-submitted candidates

summary.core_problem: OpenClaw 生态的现有评测偏“助理型任务”，缺少对真实学术/专业工作流中高难度、长时程、强执行约束任务的系统评估。论文要解决的是：如何构建一个来源真实、难度自然对齐前沿能力、并且可在 Docker 沙箱内可验证评分的 academic-level agent benchmark。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练研究的直接相关性一般，但对 post-train（agent SFT/RL）、长时程能力诊断与数据合成方向有现实价值：它提供了更“硬”的任务分布（含 GPU/CUDA 执行、跨框架调试、形式化推理等），以及多维度验证方式，能更清晰地区分模型在工具使用、形式推理、执行鲁棒性上的短板。它也提示一个常见误区：token 消耗与质量几乎不相关，单纯拉长思考/轨迹并不等价于更好策略。
summary.technical_approach:
1) 任务来源：采用 bottom-up 收集，让本科生提交“他们亲自尝试过、现有 agent 做不好”的真实学术工作流任务；从 230 个候选经专家审核筛到 80 个最终任务，覆盖 25+ 领域，双语。
2) 执行与隔离：每个任务封装在隔离的 Docker 容器内，包含提示、参考材料与评分脚本/规程；其中 16 个任务需要 CUDA GPU 执行，这在同类 agent benchmark 中较少见。
3) 评分体系：不是单一 pass/fail，而是组合六类验证信号：确定性检查、代码执行、LLM-as-judge、VLM 评估、端到端浏览器测试、结构化输出校验；并配套安全审计维度。
4) 统一评测协议：在同一 OpenClaw agent 框架下评测多家前沿模型，分析总体通过率、任务级别的能力边界、行为模式差异（read-first / execute-first / minimalist）与 token-质量关系。
summary.experiments:
评测对象包含 Claude Opus 4.6、Claude Sonnet 4.6、GPT-5.4、Gemini 3.1 Pro、Qwen3.5-397B、MiniMax M2.7。在该基准上，最佳模型通过率约 55%（以 score≥75/100 计）。
更细的诊断结论：
- 约 22% 的任务在不同模型间出现最高约 90 分的巨大分差，显示明显 capability boundary。
- 生成式任务相对更好，形式化推理（如奥赛级题）普遍失败。
- token 消耗跨模型差异超过 5×，但与质量几乎零相关（r≈-0.03）。
（若需要更贴近“预训练研究”的可用信号，建议进一步查看：哪些任务类型对模型规模/训练数据更敏感，是否提供轨迹与中间产物以支持 error attribution。）
summary.reading_guide:
泛读建议：
- 先看任务收集与筛选流程（能判断任务分布是否“可复现、可扩展”）。
- 再看评分与验证设计（六种验证如何组合、各自覆盖的失败模式、LLM-as-judge 的偏差控制）。
- 最后看模型对比与现象分析：capability boundary、三类行为 phenotype、token-质量脱钩。
预计 40-60 分钟可读完并抓住 benchmark 设计要点；若要用它做训练闭环（数据合成/RL），需要进一步深挖任务可程序化分解与奖励信号落地方式。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing OpenClaw benchmarks largely target assistant-like tasks and under-measure academic/professional workflows that are long-horizon, execution-heavy, and domain-intensive. The paper builds an academic-level benchmark with real user-sourced tasks and robust, sandboxed verification.
summary_en.importance: Its relevance to core pretraining is moderate, but it is practically useful for agent post-training (SFT/RL), long-horizon diagnostics, and data-generation pipelines. It offers a harder task distribution (including CUDA/GPU execution and cross-stack debugging) and multi-signal evaluation that better separates weaknesses in tool use, formal reasoning, and execution robustness. A notable empirical warning is that more tokens/longer traces do not reliably translate into higher quality (near-zero token–quality correlation).
summary_en.technical_approach:
1) Bottom-up task sourcing: undergraduate students submit tasks from real academic workflows that current agents fail on; 230 candidates are expert-reviewed down to 80 bilingual tasks spanning 25+ domains.
2) Sandboxed execution: each task runs in an isolated Docker container with prompts, reference materials, and evaluation procedures; 16 tasks require CUDA GPU execution.
3) Multi-dimensional scoring: combine six verification mechanisms—deterministic checks, code execution, LLM-as-judge, VLM-based assessment, end-to-end browser testing, and structured-output validation—plus safety auditing.
4) Standardized evaluation: benchmark multiple frontier models under the same OpenClaw agent framework; analyze aggregate pass rates, task-level capability boundaries, behavioral phenotypes (read-first / execute-first / minimalist), and token usage vs quality.
summary_en.experiments:
